title.en: Volume 289 Biographies 76: Zhu Shi, Xu Yuanmeng, Jiang Tingxi, Mai Zhu, Tian Congdian, Yin Tai
title.raw: 卷289 列傳七十六 朱轼 徐元梦 蒋廷锡 迈柱 田从典 尹泰

sentences.zh: 列傳七十六

translations.literal: Biographies 76
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 76

sentences.zh: 硃軾徐元夢蔣廷錫子溥邁柱白潢趙國麟

translations.literal: Zhu Shi, Xu Yuanmeng, Jiang Tingxi, his son Pu, Mai Zhu, Bai Huang, Zhao Guolin
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shi, Xu Yuanmeng, Jiang Tingxi (and his son Pu), Mai Zhu, Bai Huang, and Zhao Guolin

sentences.zh: 田從典子懋高其位遜柱尹泰陳元龍

translations.literal: Tian Congdian, his son Mao, Gao Qiwei, Sun Zhu, Yin Tai, Chen Yuanlong
translations.idiomatic: Tian Congdian (and his son Mao), Gao Qiwei, Sun Zhu, Yin Tai, and Chen Yuanlong

sentences.zh: 硃軾，字若瞻，江西高安人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shi, style name Ruozhan, was a native of Gao'an in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shi, whose style was Ruozhan, came from Gao'an in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, he ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1693 he took first place in the provincial civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，成進士，改庶吉士，散館授湖北潛江知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he became a jinshi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed magistrate of Qianjiang in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the palace examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after completing his term there was posted as magistrate of Qianjiang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 潛江俗敝賦繁，軾令免耗羨，用法必持平。

translations.literal: Qianjiang had corrupt customs and heavy taxes; Shi ordered the abolition of surcharges and miscellaneous levies, and in applying the law he always held to fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Qianjiang was plagued by corrupt local practice and crushing levies. Shi abolished surcharges and miscellaneous fees, and whenever he applied the law he insisted on even-handed justice.

sentences.zh: 有鬥毆殺人獄，上官改故殺，軾力爭之，卒莫能奪。

translations.literal: In a case of killing in a brawl, his superior changed the charge to premeditated murder; Shi argued forcefully against it, and in the end none could overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: In a homicide arising from a brawl, his superior reclassified the charge as premeditated murder. Shi fought the change vigorously and ultimately could not be overruled.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，行取，授刑部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was selected for capital office and appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, rising in stages to department director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1705 he was selected for service in the capital, appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, and eventually promoted to department director.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，出督陝西學政。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he went out as educational commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1709 he was sent out as educational commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 修橫渠張子之教，以知禮成性、變化氣質訓士。

translations.literal: He restored the teaching of Master Zhang of Hengqu, instructing scholars through knowing ritual, completing one's nature, and transforming one's temperament.
translations.idiomatic: He revived the teachings of Zhang Zai of Hengqu, training students in ritual knowledge, the completion of moral nature, and the refinement of character.

sentences.zh: 故事，試冊報部科，當有公使錢。

translations.literal: By precedent, when examination registers were reported to the ministry, there should have been envoy fees.
translations.idiomatic: According to established practice, reporting examination registers to the ministry entitled the commissioner to a per-candidate allowance.

sentences.zh: 軾獨無，坐遲誤被劾，士論為不平。

translations.literal: Shi alone took none, and on the charge of delay was impeached; scholarly opinion deemed this unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Shi alone refused such payments. He was impeached for delaying the reports, and educated opinion widely regarded this as unfair.

sentences.zh: 會有以其事聞上者，上命軾畢試事。

translations.literal: When someone reported the matter to the throne, the emperor ordered Shi to complete the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Someone eventually brought the matter to the emperor's attention, and the emperor ordered Shi to finish the examination cycle.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，擢光祿寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1713 he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 歷奉天府尹、通政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as governor of Fengtian Prefecture and commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as governor of Fengtian Prefecture and as commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，授浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was appointed governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1717 he was appointed governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，疏請修築海塘：北岸海寧老鹽倉千三百四十丈，南岸上虞夏蓋山千七百九十丈；

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he memorialized requesting repair of the seawalls: on the north bank at Laoyancang in Haining, 1,340 zhang; on the south bank at Xiagai Mountain in Shangyu, 1,790 zhang;
translations.idiomatic: In 1718 he submitted a memorial requesting seawall repairs: 1,340 zhang along the north bank at Laoyancang in Haining, and 1,790 zhang along the south bank at Xiagai Mountain in Shangyu;

sentences.zh: 並議開中亹淤沙，复江海故道。

translations.literal: and also proposed dredging the silt of the central shoal to restore the old river and sea channels.
translations.idiomatic: he also proposed dredging the central shoal's silt deposits to reopen the former river and sea channels.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「海寧沿塘皆浮沙，雖長椿巨石，難期保固。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "Along the seawalls at Haining all is loose sand; even with long piles and massive stones, lasting solidity is hard to expect.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "The ground along Haining's seawalls is all loose sand. Even long piles and massive stones cannot be expected to hold permanently.

sentences.zh: 當用水櫃法，以鬆、杉木為匱，實碎石，用為塘根，上施巨石為塘身。

translations.literal: The water-chest method should be used: making chests of pine and cedar, filling them with broken stone for the foundation of the wall, and placing massive stones above as the body of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The water-chest method should be used: pine and cedar boxes filled with broken stone should form the foundation, with massive stones laid above as the wall proper.

sentences.zh: 附塘為坦坡，亦用水櫃，外砌巨石二三重，高及塘之半，用護塘址。

translations.literal: Beside the wall a gentle slope should be made, also using water chests, with two or three layers of massive stones on the outside reaching half the height of the wall, to protect the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: A gentle slope should be built alongside the wall, likewise using water chests, with two or three tiers of massive stones on the outer face rising to half the wall's height to shield the foundation.

sentences.zh: 塘內為河，名曰備塘河。

translations.literal: Inside the wall a river should be made, called the reserve seawall river.
translations.idiomatic: A channel should be dug inside the wall, to be called the Reserve Seawall River.

sentences.zh: 居民築壩積淤，應去壩濬河，即以其土培岸。」

translations.literal: Where residents had built dams to accumulate silt, the dams should be removed and the river dredged, using that earth to build up the banks."
translations.idiomatic: Where residents had thrown up dams to trap silt, those dams should be removed, the channel dredged, and the excavated earth used to raise the banks."

sentences.zh: 俱下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 杭州南、北兩關稅，例由巡撫監收。

translations.literal: The customs duties at the southern and northern passes of Hangzhou were by precedent collected under the governor's supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Customs duties at Hangzhou's southern and northern passes were customarily collected under the governor's supervision.

sentences.zh: 軾以稅口五十餘，稽察匪易，請委員兼理。

translations.literal: Shi, because there were more than fifty tax stations and inspection was not easy, requested that commissioners be appointed to assist in management.
translations.idiomatic: Because there were more than fifty tax stations and thorough inspection was impracticable, Shi asked that additional commissioners be appointed to share the work.

sentences.zh: 部議以杭州捕盜同知監收，仍令巡撫統轄。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that the subprefect of Hangzhou for bandit suppression should supervise collection, while the governor still held overall jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that the Hangzhou subprefect responsible for bandit suppression should supervise collection, while the governor retained overall authority.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，疏劾巡鹽御史哈爾金索商人賄，上命尚書張廷樞、學士德音按治，論如律。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he memorialized impeaching the salt-circuit censor Harjin for demanding bribes from merchants; the emperor ordered Minister Zhang Tinglu and Academician Deyin to investigate, and they sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1719 he impeached the salt-circuit censor Harjin for extorting bribes from merchants. The emperor sent Minister Zhang Tinglu and Academician Deyin to investigate, and the case was decided according to law.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1720 he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遭父喪，命在任守制，疏辭，上不許，請從軍自效。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he suffered his father's death; he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office, memorialized to decline, the emperor did not permit it, and he requested to serve in the army to prove his worth.
translations.idiomatic: In 1721 his father died. He was ordered to observe mourning without leaving his post; he memorialized to decline, but the emperor refused. He then asked to join the army and prove his worth in the field.

sentences.zh: 上以山、陝旱災，發帑五十萬，命軾與光祿寺卿盧詢分往勸糶治賑。

translations.literal: Because of drought disaster in Shanxi and Shaanxi, the emperor disbursed 500,000 taels from the treasury and ordered Shi and Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Lu Xun to go separately to encourage grain sales and administer relief.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck Shanxi and Shaanxi, the emperor released 500,000 taels from the treasury and sent Shi and Lu Xun, director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, to encourage grain sales and organize relief in the two provinces.

sentences.zh: 軾往山西，疏請令被劾司道以下出資贍饑民，富民與商人出資於南省糴米，暫停淮安、鳳陽等關米稅；

translations.literal: Shi went to Shanxi and memorialized requesting that impeached officials from circuit intendant down contribute funds to support the starving, that wealthy households and merchants contribute funds to purchase rice in the southern provinces, and that the rice tax at Huai'an, Fengyang, and other passes be temporarily suspended;
translations.idiomatic: Shi went to Shanxi and proposed that impeached officials from circuit intendant rank downward contribute to feeding the hungry, that wealthy households and merchants fund rice purchases in the south, and that the rice levy at Huai'an, Fengyang, and other passes be suspended temporarily;

sentences.zh: 饑民流徙，令所在地方官安置，能出資以贍者得題薦；

translations.literal: for famine refugees who drifted about, local officials were to settle them, and those able to contribute funds for their support could be recommended for promotion;
translations.idiomatic: for refugees on the move, local officials were to provide settlement, and those who could fund relief for them were to be recommended for promotion;

sentences.zh: 饑民群聚，易生癘疫，設廠醫治。

translations.literal: when famine victims gathered in crowds, pestilence was easily generated, and clinics should be set up for treatment.
translations.idiomatic: and where hungry people gathered in large numbers, clinics should be established to treat the epidemics that so easily followed.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「倉庾積貯，有司平日侵蝕，遇災复假平糶、借貸、煮粥為名，以少報多，有名無實。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "In granary storage, officials in ordinary times embezzle; when disaster comes they again use the names of fair-price sales, loans, and porridge kitchens, reporting much from little, with name but no reality.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "Granary stocks are routinely embezzled by officials. When disaster strikes they invoke fair-price sales, loans, and free kitchens, reporting large disbursements for small ones—forms without substance.

sentences.zh: 請敕詳察虧空，少則勒限補還，多則嚴究治罪。

translations.literal: I request an imperial order for thorough investigation of deficits; where small, compel repayment within a deadline; where large, strictly investigate and punish by law.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that deficits be thoroughly investigated: minor shortfalls should be repaid within a fixed deadline; major ones should be prosecuted to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 至因賑動倉穀，輒稱捐俸抵補，俸銀有限，倉穀甚多。

translations.literal: As for moving granary grain because of relief, they always claim salary donations to make up the deficit; salary silver is limited, but granary grain is very much.
translations.idiomatic: When relief draws on granary stocks, officials routinely claim they will make up the loss from donated salaries—but official salaries are limited while granary grain is not.

sentences.zh: 借非實借，還非實還，宜並清覈。」

translations.literal: Borrowing is not real borrowing, and repayment is not real repayment; all should be cleared and audited together."
translations.idiomatic: Loans are not real loans and repayments are not real repayments. All such accounts should be audited and cleared."

sentences.zh: 皆從所議行。

translations.literal: All were adopted as proposed and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were adopted and implemented.

sentences.zh: 別疏請令山西各縣建社倉，引泉溉田。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he requested that each county in Shanxi build community granaries and draw springs to irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he asked that every county in Shanxi establish community granaries and channel springs for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「社倉始於硃子，僅可行於小縣鄉村。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Community granaries began with Master Zhu and can only be practiced in small counties and villages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Community granaries were Zhu Xi's invention and work only in small counties and rural communities.

sentences.zh: 若奏為定例，官吏奉行，久之，與民無益。

translations.literal: If memorialized as a fixed regulation for officials to carry out, in time it will benefit the people not at all.
translations.idiomatic: If this is made a standing regulation for officials to enforce, in time it will do the people no good at all.

sentences.zh: 山、陝山多水少，間有泉源，亦不能暢引溉田。

translations.literal: Shanxi and Shaanxi have many mountains and little water; even where springs exist, they cannot be freely channeled to irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi and Shaanxi are mountainous and short of water. Even where springs exist, they cannot readily be channeled for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 軾既以為請，即令久駐山西，鼓勵試行。」

translations.literal: Since Shi has already requested this, let him remain long in Shanxi and encourage trial implementation."
translations.idiomatic: Since Shi has already proposed this, let him remain in Shanxi for an extended period and encourage trial implementation there.

sentences.zh: 軾自承冒昧，乞寢其議，上不許。

translations.literal: Shi himself acknowledged his presumption and begged to shelve the proposal; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi then confessed his proposal had been rash and asked that it be withdrawn. The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，川陝總督年羹堯劾西安知府徐容、鳳翔知府甘文煊虧帑，請特簡親信大臣會鞫。

translations.literal: Before long, Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Nian Gengyao impeached Xi'an Prefect Xu Rong and Fengxiang Prefect Gan Wenxuan for treasury deficits and requested that a specially selected trusted minister jointly try the case.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general Nian Gengyao impeached Xu Rong, prefect of Xi'an, and Gan Wenxuan, prefect of Fengxiang, for treasury deficits, and asked that a specially chosen trusted minister be sent to join the investigation.

sentences.zh: 上命軾往勘，得實，論如律。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shi to go and investigate; the charges were found true, and they were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shi to investigate. The charges proved true, and both men were sentenced according to law.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，乞假葬父，歸。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he requested leave to bury his father and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1722 he asked for leave to bury his father and returned home.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，召詣京師，充聖祖實錄總裁，賜第。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded, Shi was summoned to the capital, made chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Holy Ancestor, and granted a residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor came to the throne, Shi was summoned to the capital, appointed chief compiler of the Kangxi emperor's veritable records, and given an official residence.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命直南書房。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was ordered to attend duty in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1723 he was assigned to regular duty in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 予其母冷氏封。

translations.literal: His mother, née Leng, was granted a title.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Leng, was granted an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 加吏部尚書銜，尋復加太子太保。

translations.literal: He was given the rank of minister of personnel, and soon after was further given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He received the concurrent rank of minister of personnel, and soon afterward was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 充順天鄉試考官，嘉其公慎，進太子太傅。

translations.literal: He served as examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination; the emperor praised his fairness and caution and promoted him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: As examiner for the metropolitan provincial examination he was praised for fairness and care, and was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he concurrently held the post of minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1724 he was appointed concurrent minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 命勘江、浙海塘。

translations.literal: He was ordered to survey the seawalls of Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to inspect the seawalls of Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 三年，還，奏：「浙江餘姚滸山鎮西至臨山衛，舊土塘三道，本為民灶修築。

translations.literal: In the third year he returned and reported: "From Hushen Town west in Yuyao, Zhejiang, to Linshan Guard, there are three old earthen seawalls originally built by the salt-producing households.
translations.idiomatic: In 1725 he returned and reported: "From Hushen Town west in Yuyao, Zhejiang, to Linshan Guard, three old earthen seawalls were originally built by the salt-producing households.

sentences.zh: 今民灶無力，應動帑興修。

translations.literal: Now the salt households lack the means, and treasury funds should be used to undertake repairs.
translations.idiomatic: They can no longer afford the work, and repairs should be funded from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 自臨衛經上虞烏盆村至會稽瀝海所，土塘七千丈，應以石為基，就石累土。

translations.literal: From Linshan Guard through Wupen Village in Shangyu to the Lihai Office in Kuaiji, an earthen wall of seven thousand zhang should have stone as its foundation, piling earth upon the stone.
translations.idiomatic: From Linshan Guard through Wupen Village in Shangyu to the Lihai salt office in Kuaiji, a 7,000-zhang earthen wall should be given a stone foundation with earth piled on top.

sentences.zh: 又海寧陳文港至尖山，土塘七百六十六丈，應就塘加寬，覆條石於巔，塘外以亂石為子塘，護塘址當修砌完固。

translations.literal: Also from Chenwengang to Jianshan in Haining, an earthen wall of 766 zhang should be widened on the existing wall, with strip stones laid on the crest; outside the wall loose stones should form a subsidiary wall, and the foot of the wall should be repaired and built solid.
translations.idiomatic: From Chenwengang to Jianshan in Haining, a 766-zhang earthen wall should be widened, its crest capped with strip stones, and a subsidiary wall of loose stone built outside; the foundation must be repaired and made solid.

sentences.zh: 至子塘處，依式興築。

translations.literal: Where subsidiary walls are needed, they should be built according to the prescribed method.
translations.idiomatic: Where subsidiary walls are required, they should be built to the same standard.

sentences.zh: 海鹽秦駐山至演武場石塘，圮八十丈，潰七十丈，均補築。

translations.literal: The stone seawall from Qinzhu Mountain to the drill ground in Haiyan had collapsed for 80 zhang and breached for 70 zhang; all should be repaired and rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: The stone seawall from Qinzhu Mountain to the drill ground in Haiyan had collapsed over 80 zhang and breached over 70 zhang; all damaged sections should be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 都計工需十五萬有奇。

translations.literal: In all the works would require somewhat more than 150,000 [taels].
translations.idiomatic: The total estimated cost for Zhejiang was somewhat more than 150,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 江南金山衛城北至上海華家角，土塘六千二百餘丈，內三千八百丈當改為石塘。

translations.literal: From north of Jinshan Guard in Jiangnan to Huajiajiao in Shanghai, earthen walls of more than 6,200 zhang, of which 3,800 zhang should be converted to stone walls.
translations.idiomatic: From north of Jinshan Guard in Jiangnan to Huajiajiao in Shanghai, more than 6,200 zhang of earthen wall stood, of which 3,800 zhang should be converted to stone.

sentences.zh: 上海汛頭墩至嘉定二千四百丈，水勢稍緩，土塘加築高厚，足資捍禦。

translations.literal: From Xuntoudun in Shanghai to Jiading, 2,400 zhang; the water force is somewhat gentler, and the earthen wall should be built higher and thicker, sufficient to provide defense.
translations.idiomatic: From Xuntoudun in Shanghai to Jiading, 2,400 zhang where the current is gentler, the earthen wall need only be raised and thickened to provide adequate defense.

sentences.zh: 都計工需十九萬有奇。」

translations.literal: In all the works would require somewhat more than 190,000 [taels]."
translations.idiomatic: The total estimated cost for Jiangnan was somewhat more than 190,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: This was referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: These proposals were referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 拜文華殿大學士，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall, concurrently minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall while retaining the concurrent post of minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 上命怡親王胤祥總理畿輔水利營田，以軾副之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Prince Yi Yinxiang to take general charge of water conservancy and military colonies in the capital region, with Shi as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Prince Yi, Yinxiang, in charge of waterworks and military colonies in the capital region, with Shi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 四年，請分設四局，各以道員領其事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he requested establishing four separate bureaus, each led by a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1726 he proposed dividing the work into four bureaus, each headed by a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 二月，軾遭母喪，命馳驛回籍，諭曰：「軾事母至孝，但母年八十餘，祿養顯揚，俱無餘憾。

translations.literal: In the second month Shi suffered his mother's death; he was ordered to return home by express relay, with an edict saying: "Shi served his mother with utmost filial piety, but his mother was over eighty, and in salary support and honoring her name he leaves no regret.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month his mother died. He was ordered home by express relay, with an edict saying: "Shi served his mother with the utmost devotion. She was over eighty, and he had supported and honored her without regret.

sentences.zh: 當節哀抑慟，護惜此身，為國家出力。」

translations.literal: He should restrain his grief and suppress his anguish, cherish this body, and exert strength for the state."
translations.idiomatic: He should moderate his grief, guard his health, and continue to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 賜內帑治喪，敕江西巡撫俟軾至家賜祭。

translations.literal: He was granted funds from the inner treasury for the funeral, and the Jiangxi governor was ordered to perform the sacrificial rites when Shi reached home.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial funds from the privy purse were granted for the funeral, and the Jiangxi governor was instructed to conduct the sacrificial rites when Shi arrived home.

sentences.zh: 軾奏謝，乞終制，上允解任，仍領水利營田，期八月詣京師。

translations.literal: Shi memorialized thanks, begged to complete the full mourning period, the emperor permitted him to resign his post but still to lead water conservancy and military colonies, with the expectation that in the eighth month he would come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shi thanked the emperor and asked to observe the full mourning period. The emperor allowed him to step down from office but to retain charge of waterworks and military colonies, with orders to return to the capital in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 九月，軾將至，遣學士何國宗、副都統永福迎勞，許素服終喪。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, as Shi was about to arrive, Academician He Guozong and Vice Banner Commander Yongfu were sent to welcome and comfort him; he was permitted to wear plain mourning garb until mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, as Shi was nearing the capital, Academician He Guozong and Vice Banner Commander Yongfu were sent to welcome him. He was permitted to wear plain mourning dress until the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 上以浙江風俗澆漓，特設觀風整俗使，軾疏言：「風俗澆漓，莫甚於爭訟。

translations.literal: Because Zhejiang customs were dissolute, the emperor specially established a commissioner to observe customs and rectify morals; Shi memorialized: "Of dissolute customs, none is worse than litigation.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhejiang's customs were considered corrupt, the emperor created a special commissioner to observe local morals and reform conduct. Shi wrote: "Of all signs of moral decay, none is worse than litigation.

sentences.zh: 臣巡撫​​浙江，知杭、嘉、湖、紹四府民最好訟。

translations.literal: When I was governor of Zhejiang, I knew that the people of the four prefectures Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing were most fond of lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: When I served as governor of Zhejiang, I found that the people of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing were the most litigious in the province.

sentences.zh: 請增設杭嘉湖巡道，而以紹興屬寧台道。

translations.literal: I request adding a Hang-Jia-Hu circuit for patrol, and placing Shaoxing under the Ning-Tai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: I propose creating a separate Hang-Jia-Hu circuit and placing Shaoxing under the Ning-Tai circuit.

sentences.zh: 民間詞訟冤抑，準巡道申理。」

translations.literal: For civil lawsuits in which the people suffered injustice, the circuit intendant should be allowed to hear and decide them."
translations.idiomatic: Civil suits in which common people had suffered injustice should be referred to the circuit intendant for review.

sentences.zh: 上從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病乞解任，上手詔留之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on grounds of illness he requested to resign his post; the emperor personally edicted that he remain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728, citing illness, he asked to resign. The emperor personally ordered him to stay in office.

sentences.zh: 八年，怡親王薨，命軾總理水利營田。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Prince Yi died; Shi was ordered to take general charge of water conservancy and military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1730, when Prince Yi died, Shi was put in sole charge of waterworks and military colonies.

sentences.zh: 尋兼兵部尚書，署翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: Soon after he concurrently held the post of minister of war and acted as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added the concurrent post of minister of war and served as acting chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 十三年，議築浙江海塘，軾請往董其役，上俞之，敕督撫及管理塘工諸大臣咸聽節制。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when construction of Zhejiang seawalls was discussed, Shi requested to go and supervise the work; the emperor approved, ordering governors-general, governors, and all ministers managing seawall works to obey his direction.
translations.idiomatic: In 1735, when Zhejiang's seawalls were to be rebuilt, Shi asked to supervise the project in person. The emperor agreed and ordered governors and all officials in charge of seawall works to follow his instructions.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，召還，命協同總理事務，予拜他喇布勒哈番世職。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor acceded, Shi was recalled and ordered to assist in managing affairs, and was granted the hereditary rank of Beitelabuleha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor came to the throne, Shi was recalled to assist in managing state affairs and granted the hereditary rank of Beitelabuleha Fan.

sentences.zh: 時治獄尚刻深，各省爭言開墾為民累，軾疏言：「四川丈量，多就熟田增加錢糧；

translations.literal: At that time judicial administration favored severity, and every province competed to report land reclamation as a burden on the people; Shi memorialized: "In Sichuan's land survey, they often increased tax assessments on already cultivated fields;
translations.idiomatic: At the time courts favored harsh justice, and every province was competing to report land reclamation in ways that burdened the people. Shi wrote: "In Sichuan's land surveys, officials often raised tax assessments on fields already under cultivation;

sentences.zh: 廣西報部墾田數万畝，其實多系虛無。

translations.literal: Guangxi reported to the ministry tens of thousands of mu of reclaimed land, but in fact most was empty and false.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi reported tens of thousands of mu of reclaimed land to the ministry, but most of these figures were fictitious.

sentences.zh: 因請通行丈量，冀求熟田弓口之餘，以補報墾無著之數。

translations.literal: Therefore they requested general land surveys, hoping to find surplus from the measuring cords on cultivated fields to make up the numbers of reported but unsubstantiated reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials therefore called for province-wide surveys, hoping to find marginal acreage on cultivated fields to offset fictitious reclamation figures.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝洞燭其弊，飭停止丈量；

translations.literal: The late emperor clearly saw these abuses and ordered surveys stopped;
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor saw through these abuses and ordered the surveys halted;

sentences.zh: 而前此虛報昇科，入冊輸糧，小民不免苦累。

translations.literal: yet the earlier false reports of promotion to taxation, entered in registers and paying grain, could not but impose hardship on the common people.
translations.idiomatic: but the earlier false promotions to taxable status, entered in the registers and levied in grain, still imposed hardship on common people.

sentences.zh: 河南報墾亦多不實。

translations.literal: Henan's reported reclamation was also largely untrue.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's reclamation reports were likewise largely false.

sentences.zh: 州縣田地間有未能耕種之處，或因山區磽確，旋墾旋荒；

translations.literal: Among prefectural and county fields there were places that could not be cultivated, some because mountain districts were barren and hard, reclaimed one year and abandoned the next;
translations.idiomatic: In prefectures and counties some land simply could not be farmed—mountain districts might be too barren to sustain cultivation, reclaimed one year and abandoned the next;

sentences.zh: 或因江岸河濱，東坍西漲。

translations.literal: some because along river banks and shores, land collapsed on one side and rose on the other.
translations.idiomatic: or riverbanks might shift as land eroded on one side and built up on the other.

sentences.zh: 是以荒者未盡開墾，墾者未盡昇科。

translations.literal: Thus wasteland was not fully reclaimed, and reclaimed land was not fully promoted to taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus wasteland was not fully reclaimed, and reclaimed land was not fully brought onto the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 至已熟之田，或糧額甚輕，亦由土壤磽瘠，數畝不敵腴田​​一畝，非欺隱者比。

translations.literal: As for already cultivated fields, some had very light tax quotas, also because the soil was barren and poor, and several mu did not equal one mu of fertile land—this was not comparable to concealment and evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Some already cultivated fields carried very light tax quotas because the soil was so poor that several mu were worth less than one mu of fertile land—this was not concealment or fraud.

sentences.zh: 不但丈量不可行，即令據實首報，小民惟恐察出治罪，勉強報升，將來完納不前，仍歸荒廢。

translations.literal: Not only were surveys unworkable; even if truthful reporting were ordered, common people would only fear discovery and punishment, force themselves to report promotion, and in the future when payment could not be completed, the land would return to waste.
translations.idiomatic: Surveys were not merely impracticable: even honest reporting would frighten common people into inflating reclamation figures for fear of punishment, and when they could not pay the taxes the land would fall back into waste.

sentences.zh: 請停止丈量，飭禁首報，詳察現在報墾之田，有不實者，題請開除。」

translations.literal: I request stopping surveys, forbidding voluntary reports of promotion, and thoroughly investigating presently reported reclaimed fields; where untrue, memorializing for removal from the registers."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that surveys be halted, voluntary promotion reports forbidden, and all currently registered reclaimed land carefully investigated; where reports are false, memorials should be submitted to strike the land from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「法吏以嚴刻為能，不問是非曲直，刻意株​​連，惟逞鍛鍊之長，希著明察之號。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "Legal officials take severity as ability, without asking right from wrong, deliberately implicating others by association, only displaying their skill in forced confessions, hoping to win a reputation for keen discernment.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote: "Judicial officials treat harshness as competence. Without regard for right or wrong, they deliberately implicate others, display their skill at extracting confessions, and hope to win a reputation for penetrating insight.

sentences.zh: 請敕督撫諭有司，讞獄務虛公詳慎，原情酌理，協於中正。

translations.literal: I request an imperial order to governors-general and governors to instruct subordinate officials that in deciding cases they must be impartial, thorough, and cautious, considering the original circumstances and weighing reason, conforming to the mean.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governors-general and governors instruct their subordinates to decide cases with impartial care, weigh the original circumstances, and keep to the middle way of justice.

sentences.zh: 刑具悉遵定制，不得擅用夾棍、大枷。」

translations.literal: All instruments of punishment should follow the established regulations; they must not on their own authority use leg-crushing sticks or large cangues."
translations.idiomatic: All instruments of punishment must follow the established regulations. Officials must not on their own authority use leg-crushing sticks or large cangues.

sentences.zh: 上深嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly approved both memorials.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，充世宗實錄總裁。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Shizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he was appointed chief compiler of the Yongzheng emperor's veritable records.

sentences.zh: 九月，病篤，上親臨視疾。

translations.literal: In the ninth month his illness became grave; the emperor personally came to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month his illness turned critical, and the emperor came in person to see him.

sentences.zh: 軾力疾服朝服，令其子扶掖，迎拜戶外。

translations.literal: Shi, forcing himself despite illness, put on court dress, had his son support him, and went out to bow in welcome outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: Despite his weakness Shi donned court dress, had his son support him, and went out to bow in welcome at the gate.

sentences.zh: 翌日，卒。

translations.literal: The next day he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following day.

sentences.zh: 遺疏略言：「萬事根本君心，用人理財，尤宜慎重。

translations.literal: His final memorial briefly stated: "In all affairs the root lies in the sovereign's mind; in employing men and managing finances, especial care is needed.
translations.idiomatic: In his final memorial he wrote in brief: "In all affairs the sovereign's judgment is the foundation. In appointing men and managing finances, the utmost care is required.

sentences.zh: 君子小人，公私邪正，判在幾微，當審察其心跡而進退之。

translations.literal: Gentleman and petty man, public and private, straight and crooked, are distinguished in the subtlest signs; one should carefully examine their hearts and conduct in promoting or dismissing them.
translations.idiomatic: The distinction between the worthy and the base, between public duty and private interest, between the upright and the corrupt, turns on the subtlest signs. Their hearts and conduct should be carefully weighed before they are advanced or removed.

sentences.zh: 至國家經費，本自有餘，異日倘有言利之臣，倡加賦之稅，伏祈聖心乾斷，永斥浮言，實四海蒼生之福。」

translations.literal: As for state revenue, it is in itself already sufficient; if in future there should be profit-seeking ministers advocating increased taxes, I humbly pray that Your Sacred Mind decide firmly, forever rejecting empty talk—this would truly be the blessing of all the people within the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: As for state revenue, the treasury is already ample. If someday profit-seeking ministers should advocate new taxes, I pray that Your Majesty decide firmly and forever reject such proposals. That would be a true blessing for all the people under heaven.

sentences.zh: 上震悼輟朝，复親臨致奠，發帑治喪。

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken with grief, suspended court, again came in person to offer sacrifices, and disbursed treasury funds for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved, suspended court, came again in person to offer sacrifices, and released treasury funds for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，賜祭葬，諡文端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, granted sacrificial funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, granted state funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Wenduan, "Cultured and Upright."

sentences.zh: 軾樸誠事主，純修清德，負一時重望。

translations.literal: Shi was plain and sincere in serving his lord, purely cultivated in clear virtue, and bore the heavy expectations of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Shi served his sovereign with plain sincerity, cultivated pure integrity, and commanded the highest respect of his generation.

sentences.zh: 高宗初典學，世宗命為師傅，設席懋勤殿，行拜師禮。

translations.literal: When Gaozong first took charge of his studies, Shizong ordered Shi as his tutor; a seat was set in the Maojin Hall and the ceremony of bowing to the teacher was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong first began his studies, the Yongzheng emperor appointed Shi as his tutor. A seat was set in the Maojin Hall and the prince performed the ceremony of bowing to his teacher.

sentences.zh: 軾以經訓進講，亟稱賈、董、宋五子之學。

translations.literal: Shi lectured on the basis of classical instruction and repeatedly praised the learning of Jia, Dong, and the Five Masters of the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Shi lectured from the classics and repeatedly commended the learning of Jia Yi, Dong Zhongshu, and the Five Masters of the Song.

sentences.zh: 高宗深重之，懷舊詩稱可亭硃先生，可亭，軾號也。

translations.literal: Gaozong held him in deep esteem; in a nostalgic poem he called him Master Zhu of Keting—Keting being Shi's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong held him in the deepest regard. In a nostalgic poem he called him Master Zhu of Keting—Keting being Shi's sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 子必堦，以廕生官至大理寺卿；

translations.literal: His son Bijie, through hereditary privilege, rose to be chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: His son Bijie, entering office by hereditary privilege, rose to chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review;

sentences.zh: 璂，進士，官至左庶子；

translations.literal: Qi, a jinshi, rose to left sublector;
translations.idiomatic: Qi, a jinshi, rose to left sublector of the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 必坦，舉人，襲騎都尉。

translations.literal: Bitan, a provincial graduate, inherited the rank of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: and Bitan, a provincial graduate, inherited the rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 徐元夢，字善長，舒穆祿氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanmeng, style name Shanchang, of the Sumuru clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanmeng, whose style was Shanchang, was a Manchu of the Sumuru clan in the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年進士，改庶吉士，散館授戶部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twelfth year of Kangxi, he became a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in 1673, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after completing his term there was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷中允，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to junior compiler and served as diarist of the Daily Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1683 he was promoted to junior compiler and appointed diarist of the Daily Lecture.

sentences.zh: 尋复遷侍講。

translations.literal: Soon after he was again promoted to lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again to lecturer.

sentences.zh: 徐元夢以講學負聲譽，大學士明珠欲羅致之，其遷詞曹直講筵，明珠嘗薦於上。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanmeng had a reputation for lecturing on learning; Grand Secretary Mingzhu wished to recruit him. When he was transferred to the secretariat and attended the lecture hall, Mingzhu once recommended him to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanmeng was renowned as a lecturer. Grand Secretary Mingzhu wished to recruit him, and when Xu was transferred to the secretariat and the lecture hall, Mingzhu once recommended him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 徐元夢以明珠方擅政，不一至其門，而掌院學士李光地亦好講學，賢徐元夢及侍講學士德格勒，亟稱於上前，二人者每於上前相推獎；

translations.literal: Xu Yuanmeng, because Mingzhu was then monopolizing power, never once went to his door; but Chancellor Li Guangdi also loved lecturing, esteemed Xu Yuanmeng and Lecturer Degeli, and repeatedly praised them before the throne—the two men often commended each other before the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Because Mingzhu then monopolized power, Xu never once called at his door. Chancellor Li Guangdi also loved scholarly lecturing and esteemed Xu Yuanmeng and Lecturer Degeli, repeatedly praising both before the emperor. The two men often commended each other in the emperor's presence;

sentences.zh: 明珠黨蜚語謂與光地為黨。

translations.literal: Mingzhu's faction spread rumors that they formed a clique with Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: and Mingzhu's faction spread rumors that they were in league with Li Guangdi.

sentences.zh: 二十六年夏，上御乾清宮，召陳廷敬、湯斌、徐乾學、耿介、高士奇、孟亮揆、徐潮、徐嘉炎、熊賜瓚、勵杜訥及二人入試，題為理學真偽論。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year the emperor held court in the Qianqing Palace, summoned Chen Tingjing, Tang Bin, Xu Qianxue, Geng Jie, Gao Shiqi, Meng Liangkui, Xu Chao, Xu Jiayan, Xiong Cixuan, Li Dunuo, and the two men to take an examination on the theme "On the True and False in Neo-Confucian Learning."
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1687 the emperor held court in the Qianqing Palace and summoned Chen Tingjing, Tang Bin, Xu Qianxue, Geng Jie, Gao Shiqi, Meng Liangkui, Xu Chao, Xu Jiayan, Xiong Cixuan, Li Dunuo, and the two men to an examination on the theme "On the True and False in Neo-Confucian Learning."

sentences.zh: 方屬草，有旨詰二人，德格勒於文後申辯，徐元夢卷未竟。

translations.literal: While they were drafting, an edict rebuked the two men; Degeli appended a defense after his essay, while Xu Yuanmeng's paper was unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: While they were still writing, an edict rebuked the two men. Degeli appended a defense to his essay; Xu Yuanmeng's paper was unfinished.

sentences.zh: 上閱畢，於德格勒及賜瓚有所譙讓，命同試者互校，斌仍稱徐元夢文為是。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished reading, he reproached Degeli and Cixuan, ordered those who had taken the examination to cross-check one another, and Bin still declared Xu Yuanmeng's essay correct.
translations.idiomatic: After reading the papers, the emperor reproached Degeli and Xiong Cixuan and ordered the candidates to cross-check one another's work. Tang Bin still declared Xu Yuanmeng's essay the best.

sentences.zh: 是時斌被命輔導皇太子，尋亦命徐元夢授諸皇子讀。

translations.literal: At this time Bin was ordered to tutor the crown prince; soon Xu Yuanmeng was also ordered to teach the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Tang Bin was ordered to tutor the crown prince. Soon Xu Yuanmeng was also ordered to teach the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 秋，上御瀛台，教諸皇子射，徐元夢不能挽強，上不懌，責徐元夢​​。

translations.literal: In autumn the emperor held court at Yingtai and taught the princes archery; Xu Yuanmeng could not draw a strong bow; the emperor was displeased and reproached Xu Yuanmeng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn the emperor went to Yingtai to teach the princes archery. Xu Yuanmeng could not draw a strong bow. The emperor was displeased and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 徐元夢奏辯，上益怒，命撲之，創，遂籍其家，戍其父母。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanmeng memorialized in defense; the emperor grew angrier, ordered him beaten with the stick, inflicted wounds, then confiscated his household property and banished his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Xu memorialized in his own defense. The emperor grew angrier, ordered him beaten with the stick until he was wounded, confiscated his household property, and banished his parents.

sentences.zh: 其夜，上意解，令醫為治創。

translations.literal: That night the emperor's anger eased, and he ordered physicians to treat the wounds.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor's anger eased, and he ordered physicians to treat Xu's wounds.

sentences.zh: 翌日，命授諸皇子讀如故。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered that teaching the princes continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered that Xu resume teaching the princes as before.

sentences.zh: 徐元夢乞赦其父母，已就道，使追還。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanmeng begged pardon for his parents; they had already set out on the road, and he was ordered to bring them back.
translations.idiomatic: Xu begged pardon for his parents. They had already set out into exile, but the emperor ordered them brought back.

sentences.zh: 冬，掌院學士庫勒納奏劾德格勒私抹起居注，並言與徐元夢互相標榜，奪官逮下獄。

translations.literal: In winter Chancellor Kule'na memorialized impeaching Degeli for privately altering the Veritable Records, and also said that he and Xu Yuanmeng mutually promoted each other; their offices were stripped and they were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Chancellor Kule'na impeached Degeli for privately altering the Veritable Records and accused him and Xu Yuanmeng of mutual puffery. Both men were stripped of office and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 二十七年春，獄上，當德格勒立斬，徐元夢絞。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year the case was reported upward; Degeli was sentenced to immediate decapitation, Xu Yuanmeng to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1688 the case was reported upward. Degeli was sentenced to immediate decapitation and Xu Yuanmeng to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 上命貸徐元夢死，荷校三月，鞭百，入辛者庫。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xu Yuanmeng's death spared; he wore the cangue for three months, received a hundred lashes, and was sent to the Sinister Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared Xu's life. He wore the cangue for three months, received a hundred lashes, and was sent to the Sinister Works.

sentences.zh: 上徐察徐元夢忠誠，三十二年，命直上書房，仍授諸皇子讀。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually observed Xu Yuanmeng's loyalty; in the thirty-second year he ordered him to attend the Upper Study and again teach the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually the emperor came to see Xu's loyalty. In 1693 he was ordered back to the Upper Study to teach the princes again.

sentences.zh: 尋授內務府會計司員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed vice director in the Accounts Bureau of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice director in the Accounts Bureau of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，充順天鄉試考官。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he served as examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1702 he served as examiner for the metropolitan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 五十年，諭曰：「徐元夢繙譯，現今無能過之。」

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year an edict said: "In translation Xu Yuanmeng today has no superior."
translations.idiomatic: In 1711 the emperor declared: "In translation Xu Yuanmeng today has no equal.

sentences.zh: 授額外內閣侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed supernumerary reader of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supernumerary reader of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，充會試考官。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he served as examiner for the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1712 he served as examiner for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，擢內閣學士，歸原旗。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was promoted to grand secretary and returned to his original banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1713 he was promoted to grand secretary and returned to his original banner.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，授浙江巡撫，上諭之曰：「浙江駐防滿洲兵，爾當與將軍協同訓練。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he was appointed governor of Zhejiang; the emperor instructed him: "The Manchu garrison troops in Zhejiang—you should jointly train them with the general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1714 he was appointed governor of Zhejiang. The emperor instructed him: "You should work with the general to train the Manchu garrison troops in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 錢糧有虧空，爾宜清理，無累百姓。

translations.literal: Where grain taxes have deficits, you should clear them up without burdening the people.
translations.idiomatic: Where tax accounts show deficits, you should clear them up without burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 至於用人，當隨材器使，不可求全。」

translations.literal: As for employing men, you should assign them according to their talents and capacities, and must not demand completeness."
translations.idiomatic: In appointing men, assign each according to his talents and do not demand perfection.

sentences.zh: 賜御製詩文集及鞍馬以行。

translations.literal: He was granted the emperor's collected poems and essays and a saddle horse for his journey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him his own collected poems and essays and a saddle horse for the journey.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，疏言：「杭州、紹興等七府旱潦成災，已蒙蠲賑，並截漕平糶。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he memorialized: "Hangzhou, Shaoxing, and six other prefectures have suffered drought and flood disaster; exemption and relief have already been granted, and grain transport has been diverted for fair-price sales.
translations.idiomatic: In 1715 he memorialized: "Hangzhou, Shaoxing, and six other prefectures have suffered drought and flood. Exemptions and relief have already been granted, and grain transport has been diverted for fair-price sales.

sentences.zh: 未完額賦，尚有十三萬餘兩，請秋成後徵半，餘俟來歲。」

translations.literal: Of unpaid tax quotas there remain more than 130,000 taels; I request that after the autumn harvest half be collected, and the remainder wait until next year."
translations.idiomatic: Of unpaid tax quotas more than 130,000 taels remain. I ask that half be collected after the autumn harvest and the remainder deferred until the following year.

sentences.zh: 上允之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳修復萬松嶺書院，上賜「浙水敷文」榜，因請以敷文名書院。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting repair of the Wansongling Academy; the emperor granted the plaque "Spreading Culture on the Zhe Waters," and he therefore requested that the academy be named Fufen.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting the repair of Wansongling Academy. The emperor granted the plaque "Spreading Culture on the Zhe Waters," and Xu asked that the academy be renamed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，左都御史及翰林院掌院學士缺員，吏部以請。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year there were vacancies for left censor-in-chief and chancellor of the Hanlin Academy; the Ministry of Personnel requested instructions.
translations.idiomatic: In 1717 vacancies opened for left censor-in-chief and chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and the Ministry of Personnel asked whom to appoint.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「是當以不畏人兼學問優者任之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These posts should be filled by one who fears no man and whose learning is excellent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "These posts should go to a man who fears no one and whose learning is outstanding.

sentences.zh: 以命徐元夢。

translations.literal: He appointed Xu Yuanmeng.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xu Yuanmeng.

sentences.zh: 上諭科場積習未除，命甄別任滿學政及考官不稱職者，皆劾罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed that entrenched abuses in the examination halls had not been removed, and ordered screening of educational commissioners and examiners at the end of their terms who were unfit for office; all were impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said entrenched examination abuses had not been eliminated and ordered that educational commissioners and examiners who had completed their terms be screened; those found unfit were impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，遷工部尚書，仍兼掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was transferred to minister of works, still concurrently chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1718 he was transferred to minister of works while retaining the concurrent post of Hanlin chancellor.

sentences.zh: 六十年，上賜以詩，謂：「徐元夢乃同學舊翰林，康熙十六年以前進士祗此一人。」

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year the emperor granted him a poem, saying: "Xu Yuanmeng is an old Hanlin classmate; among jinshi before the sixteenth year of Kangxi he is the only one remaining.
translations.idiomatic: In 1721 the emperor granted him a poem, saying: "Xu Yuanmeng is an old Hanlin classmate. Among jinshi before 1677 he is the only one still living.

translations.literal: (Close of imperial quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (Close of imperial quotation.)

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，復命直上書房，授諸皇子讀。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded, Xu was again ordered to attend the Upper Study and teach the princes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor came to the throne, Xu was again ordered to the Upper Study to teach the princes.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命與大學士張鵬翮等甄別翰詹各官不稱職者，勒令解退回籍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was ordered, together with Grand Secretary Zhang Peng'e and others, to screen Hanlin and Hanlin-related officials who were unfit for office and compel them to resign and return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1723 he was ordered, together with Grand Secretary Zhang Peng'e and others, to screen Hanlin officials who were unfit for office and compel them to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 大學士富寧安出視師，命徐元夢署大學士。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Funing'an went out to inspect the army, Xu Yuanmeng was ordered to act as grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Funing'an went out to inspect the army, Xu was ordered to serve as acting grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋復命兼署左都御史，充明史總裁，調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was again ordered concurrently to act as left censor-in-chief, made chief compiler of the History of Ming, and transferred to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to serve concurrently as acting left censor-in-chief, appointed chief compiler of the History of Ming, and transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，以繙譯本章錯誤奪官，命在內閣學士之列效力行走，仍司繙譯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on account of errors in translating memorials, his office was stripped; he was ordered to serve in the ranks of grand secretaries, still in charge of translation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1726 errors in his translation of memorials cost him his office. He was ordered to serve among the grand secretaries while continuing to handle translation.

sentences.zh: 八年，复坐前在浙江失察呂留良逆書，命同繙譯中書行走。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was again punished for his earlier failure while in Zhejiang to detect the seditious books of Lü Liuliang, and was ordered to serve with the translating secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1730 he was punished again for his earlier failure in Zhejiang to detect the seditious works of Lü Liuliang and was ordered to serve with the translating secretaries.

sentences.zh: 十三年，充繙譯鄉試考官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he served as examiner for the Manchu provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1735 he served as examiner for the Manchu provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，命直南書房，尋授內閣學士。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor acceded, Xu was ordered to attend the Southern Study; soon he was appointed grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor came to the throne, Xu was assigned to the Southern Study and soon appointed grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部侍郎，以衰老不能理刑名，疏辭，調禮部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of punishments; because of age and infirmity he could not manage criminal cases, memorialized to decline, and was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of punishments but, citing age and inability to manage criminal cases, asked to be relieved and was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 充世宗實錄副總裁。

translations.literal: He served as associate chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Shizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as associate chief compiler of the Yongzheng emperor's veritable records.

sentences.zh: 詔輯八旗滿洲氏族通譜，命與鄂爾泰、福敏董其事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered compilation of the Comprehensive Genealogies of the Manchu Clans of the Eight Banners; he was ordered with Ortai and Fumin to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered compilation of the Comprehensive Genealogies of the Manchu Clans of the Eight Banners, he was ordered with Ortai and Fumin to supervise the project.

sentences.zh: 復命直上書房，課皇子讀。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to the Upper Study to instruct the princes.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to the Upper Study to instruct the princes.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，乞休，命解侍郎任，加尚書銜食俸，仍在內廷行走，領諸館事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he requested retirement; he was ordered to resign the vice ministership, given the rank of minister with salary, still to attend within the inner court, and placed in charge of all academies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he asked to retire. He was relieved of the vice ministership but given ministerial rank with salary, kept at court, and placed in charge of the academies.

sentences.zh: 二年，上臨雍，疏請以有子升堂配享，改宰我、冉求兩廡，而進南宮適、虙不齊升配。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the emperor attended the imperial lecture at the Confucian temple, Xu memorialized requesting that You Ruo be promoted to main-hall sacrifice, that Zai Wo and Ran Qiu be moved to the side halls, and that Nan Gong Kuo and Fu Buqi be advanced to main-hall sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1737, when the emperor lectured at the Confucian temple, Xu memorialized requesting that You Ruo be promoted to main-hall sacrifice, that Zai Wo and Ran Qiu be moved to the side halls, and that Nangong Kuo and Fu Buqi be advanced to main-hall sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 下大學士九卿議，以有子升祀位次子夏，餘寢未行。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers for deliberation; only You Ruo's promotion to sacrifice was approved, ranking below Zisi; the rest was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers. Only You Ruo's promotion was approved, ranking below Zisi; the rest was shelved.

sentences.zh: 复乞休，上曰：「徐元夢年雖逾八十，未甚衰憊，可量力供職。」

translations.literal: He again requested retirement; the emperor said: "Although Xu Yuanmeng is over eighty, he is not very decrepit and may continue to serve according to his strength."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire again. The emperor said: "Although Xu Yuanmeng is over eighty, he is not greatly enfeebled and may continue to serve as his strength allows.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，召同諸大臣賦柏梁體詩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he was summoned with other ministers to compose poems in the Bolang style.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1739 he was summoned with other ministers to compose poems in the Bolang style.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，疾作，遣太醫診視，賜葠藥。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year illness set in; imperial physicians were sent to examine him and ginseng medicine was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1741 he fell ill. Imperial physicians were sent to examine him and ginseng medicine was granted.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，疾劇，上諭曰：「徐元夢踐履篤實，言行相符。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter the illness grew severe; the emperor instructed: "Xu Yuanmeng's conduct is solid and sincere, his words and deeds accord.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month his illness grew critical. The emperor declared: "Xu Yuanmeng's conduct is solid and sincere; his words and deeds accord.

sentences.zh: 歷事三朝，出入禁近，小心謹慎，數十年如一日。

translations.literal: He served three reigns, entering and leaving the forbidden precincts, careful and cautious for decades as though it were a single day.
translations.idiomatic: He served three reigns in close attendance at court, careful and cautious for decades as though it were a single day.

sentences.zh: 壽逾大耋，洵屬完人。」

translations.literal: His years exceeded great old age; he was truly a complete man."
translations.idiomatic: He lived beyond great old age and was truly a man of complete virtue.

sentences.zh: 命皇長子視疾。

translations.literal: The eldest imperial son was ordered to visit him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest imperial son was ordered to visit him.

sentences.zh: 疾革，復遣使問所欲言。

translations.literal: When the illness reached its crisis, envoys were again sent to ask what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness reached its crisis, envoys were again sent to ask what he wished to say.

sentences.zh: 徐元夢伏枕流涕曰：「臣受恩重，心所欲言，口不能盡！」

translations.literal: Xu Yuanmeng, prostrate on his pillow and weeping, said: "Your servant has received heavy grace; what the heart wishes to say the mouth cannot fully express!"
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate on his pillow and weeping, Xu said: "I have received such great favor that what my heart wishes to say my mouth cannot fully express!

sentences.zh: 使出，呼曾孫取論語檢視良久。

translations.literal: When the envoy withdrew, he called his great-grandson to bring the Analects and examined it for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy withdrew, he called his great-grandson to bring the Analects and pored over it for a long while.

sentences.zh: 翌日遂卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: The next day he died, aged eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following day, aged eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上復命和親王及皇長子奠茶酒，發帑治喪。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Prince He and the eldest imperial son to offer tea and wine in sacrifice, and disbursed treasury funds for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered Prince He and the eldest imperial son to offer tea and wine in sacrifice and released treasury funds for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，賜祭葬，諡文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, granted sacrificial funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, granted state funeral honors, and given the posthumous title Wending, "Cultured and Settled."

sentences.zh: 孫舒赫德，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Shuhede has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shuhede has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 蔣廷錫，字揚孫，江南常熟人，雲貴總督陳錫弟。

translations.literal: Jiang Tingxi, style name Yangsun, was a native of Changshu in Jiangnan, younger brother of Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Chen Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tingxi, whose style was Yangsun, came from Changshu in Jiangnan and was the younger brother of Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Chen Xi.

sentences.zh: 初以舉人供奉內廷。

translations.literal: At first, as a provincial graduate, he served in attendance within the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered court service as a provincial graduate in attendance within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十二年，賜進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Kangxi he was granted jinshi status and made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1703 he was granted jinshi status and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，未散館即​​授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, before leaving the academy he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1704, before completing his Hanlin term, he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 屢遷轉至內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until he reached grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，擢禮部侍郎，世宗賜詩賢之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was promoted to vice minister of rites; Shizong granted him a poem praising his worth.
translations.idiomatic: In 1723 he was promoted to vice minister of rites, and the Yongzheng emperor granted him a poem praising his worth.

sentences.zh: 廷錫疏言：「國家廣黌序，設廩膳，以興文教，乃生員經年未嘗一至學宮。

translations.literal: Tingxi memorialized: "The state broadly extends schools, establishes stipends, to promote culture and education—yet licentiates for years never once go to the school palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang memorialized: "The state has broadly extended schools and established stipends to promote learning, yet licentiates may go years without ever setting foot in the school.

sentences.zh: 請敕學臣通飭府、州、縣、衛教官，凡所管生員，務立程課，面加考校，講究經史。

translations.literal: I request an imperial order to educational commissioners to instruct broadly the instructors of prefectures, departments, counties, and guards that for all licentiates under their charge they must establish regular lessons, examine them face to face, and study the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that educational commissioners instruct the instructors of prefectures, departments, counties, and guards to set regular lessons for all licentiates under their charge, examine them in person, and require study of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 學臣於歲、科考時，以文藝優劣定教職賢否。

translations.literal: At the annual and triennial examinations educational commissioners should determine the worth of instructors by the quality of students' literary work.
translations.idiomatic: At the annual and triennial examinations, educational commissioners should judge instructors by the quality of their students' literary work.

sentences.zh: 會典載順治九年定鄉設社學，以冒濫停止。

translations.literal: The Collected Statutes record that in the ninth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that townships should establish community schools, but because of abuse this was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Statutes record that in 1652 townships were ordered to establish community schools, but the practice was halted because of abuse.

sentences.zh: ​​請敕督撫令所屬州、縣，鄉、堡立社學，擇生員學優行端者充社師，量給廩餼。

translations.literal: I request an imperial order to governors-general and governors to have their subordinate prefectures and counties establish community schools in townships and forts, selecting licentiates of superior learning and upright conduct to serve as community teachers, and granting stipends in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that governors-general and governors order their prefectures and counties to establish community schools in townships and forts, selecting licentiates of superior learning and upright conduct as community teachers and granting them stipends in due measure.

sentences.zh: 鄉民子弟年十二以上、二十以下有志者得入學。」

translations.literal: Sons of township people between twelve and twenty who are ambitious may enter to study.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of common people between twelve and twenty who show aptitude may enroll to study.

sentences.zh: 下部議，從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was sent down to the ministry for deliberation, and they assented.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the ministry for deliberation and adopted.

sentences.zh: 二年，奏請續纂大清會典，即命為副總裁。

translations.literal: In the second year he memorialized requesting continued compilation of the Collected Statutes of the Great Qing, and was immediately appointed associate chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1724 he memorialized requesting the continued compilation of the Collected Statutes of the Great Qing and was immediately appointed associate chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 調戶部。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三年，命與內務府總管來保察閱京倉。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered, together with Laibao, superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, to inspect the capital granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1725 he was ordered to join Laibao, superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, in inspecting the capital granaries.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「漕運全資水利，宜通源節流，以濟運道。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized: "Grain transport wholly relies on water works; one should open sources and economize flow to aid the transport channel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted another memorial: "Grain transport depends entirely on water management. Sources should be opened and flow regulated to sustain the canal route.

sentences.zh: 山東漕河，取資汶、濟、洸、泗四水，而四水又賴諸泉助成巨流。

translations.literal: The grain-transport canal in Shandong draws on the four rivers Wen, Ji, Guang, and Si, and these four rivers in turn rely on the many springs to form a great flow.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's grain canal draws on the Wen, Ji, Guang, and Si rivers, which in turn depend on numerous springs to swell into a mighty current.

sentences.zh: 山東一省，得泉百有八十，其派有五，分水、天井、魯橋、新河、沂水是也。

translations.literal: In Shandong province there are one hundred and eighty springs; their branches are five, namely Fenshui, Tianjing, Luqiao, Xinhe, and Yishui.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong has one hundred and eighty springs, grouped into five branches: Fenshui, Tianjing, Luqiao, Xinhe, and Yishui.

sentences.zh: 五派合為一水，是名泉河，舊設管泉通判。

translations.literal: The five branches combine into one watercourse called the Spring River; formerly a subprefect for managing springs was established.
translations.idiomatic: These five branches merge into a single channel called the Spring River. The post of subprefect for spring management had originally been established there.

sentences.zh: 今雖裁汰，仍設泉夫。

translations.literal: Although this office has now been abolished, spring laborers are still maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Though that post has since been abolished, spring-maintenance laborers are still retained.

sentences.zh: 請飭有泉州縣，督率疏濬。

translations.literal: I request that counties possessing springs be ordered to supervise and lead dredging and clearing.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that every county with springs be ordered to oversee dredging and clearing work.

sentences.zh: 濟南、兗州二府為濟水伏流之地，若廣為濬導，則散湮沙礫間者，隨地湧見。

translations.literal: The two prefectures of Jinan and Yanzhou are places where the Ji River flows underground; if dredging and channeling are broadly carried out, those scattered and buried among sand and gravel will emerge wherever the ground permits.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan and Yanzhou prefectures lie where the Ji River runs underground. If dredging is pursued on a broad scale, springs buried among sand and gravel will reappear wherever the terrain allows.

sentences.zh: 應立法泉夫濬出新泉，優賚銀米，歲終冊報，為州縣課最。

translations.literal: Regulations should be enacted for spring laborers to dredge out new springs; silver and grain should be granted as special rewards, year-end registers reported, and this made the standard for judging prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations should require spring laborers to open new springs, with silver and grain granted as rewards. Year-end reports should be filed, and this should count toward the performance evaluation of prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 諸泉所匯，為湖十五，各設斗門為減水閘，以時啟閉。

translations.literal: The springs gather into fifteen lakes; at each a sluice gate should be set as a spillway gate, opened and closed according to season.
translations.idiomatic: The springs feed fifteen lakes, each fitted with sluice gates to release excess water, opened and closed as needed.

sentences.zh: 漕溢則減漕入湖，漕涸則啟湖濟漕，號諸湖為水櫃。

translations.literal: When the grain canal overflows, spill the excess into the lakes; when the canal runs dry, open the lakes to aid the canal—these lakes are called water cabinets.
translations.idiomatic: When the grain canal runs high, excess water is diverted into the lakes; when it runs low, the lakes supply the canal. These lakes are known as water cabinets.

sentences.zh: 其後居民壅水佔耕，壩圮閘塞，低處多生茭草，高處積沙與漕河堤並。

translations.literal: Afterward residents dammed the water and occupied land for cultivation; dikes collapsed and gates clogged; in low places wild rice grass grew abundantly, and in high places sand accumulated level with the grain-canal dike.
translations.idiomatic: Later, residents blocked water and reclaimed land for farming. Dams collapsed and sluices choked with silt. Low areas sprouted wild rice grass, while high ground piled with sand level with the canal embankment.

sentences.zh: 請察勘未耕之地，就低處挑深，即以挑出之土築堤，復水櫃之制。

translations.literal: I request inspection and survey of uncultivated land: dig deep at low places and use the excavated earth to build dikes, restoring the water-cabinet system.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that uncultivated land be surveyed, low spots dug deeper, and the excavated earth used to rebuild the embankments, restoring the water-cabinet system.

sentences.zh: 諸湖開支河，以承諸泉之入，益漕河之流，建閘以時減放。

translations.literal: Branch rivers should be opened from the lakes to receive the inflow of springs and increase the flow of the grain canal; sluice gates should be built to spill and release according to season.
translations.idiomatic: Branch channels should be cut from the lakes to receive spring inflows and boost canal flow, with sluice gates built to regulate discharge.

sentences.zh: 舊制，運河於每歲十月築壩，分洩諸湖，來春三月冰泮，開壩受水。

translations.literal: Under the old system, every year in the tenth month the Grand Canal had dikes built to divide and discharge into the various lakes; the following spring in the third month, when ice melted, the dikes were opened to receive water.
translations.idiomatic: Under the established practice, every tenth month dikes were built on the Grand Canal to divert water into the lakes; the following spring, when the ice broke in the third month, the dikes were opened to let water in.

sentences.zh: 法久玩生，築壩每至十一月，則失之遲；

translations.literal: When a rule is long enforced it breeds neglect; building dikes often waited until the eleventh month, which was too late;
translations.idiomatic: Long-standing rules breed laxity: dike-building often slipped to the eleventh month, which was too late;

sentences.zh: 開壩在正月初旬，又失之早。

translations.literal: opening the dikes in the first ten days of the first month was again too early.
translations.idiomatic: while opening them in the first ten days of the first month was too early.

sentences.zh: 請飭所司築必十月望前，開必二月朔後，以循舊制。

translations.literal: I request that responsible offices be ordered to build necessarily before the fifteenth of the tenth month and open necessarily after the first of the second month, to follow the old system.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that responsible officials be required to complete dike-building before the fifteenth of the tenth month and open the dikes only after the first of the second month, in keeping with the original schedule.

sentences.zh: 汶水分流南北，運道攸賴。

translations.literal: The Wen River divides its flow north and south; the transport route depends on it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wen River splits its flow north and south, and the canal route depends on it entirely.

sentences.zh: 明宣德間，築戴村壩於汶水南，以遏汶水入洸；

translations.literal: In the Xuande era of Ming, the Daicun Dam was built south of the Wen River to check the Wen and send it into the Guang;
translations.idiomatic: During the Ming Xuande reign, the Daicun Dam was built south of the Wen River to divert its waters into the Guang;

sentences.zh: 建坎河壩於汶水北，以節汶水歸海。

translations.literal: the Kanhe Dam was built north of the Wen River to regulate the Wen's return to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Kanhe Dam was built to the north to control the Wen River's flow to the sea.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，复堆積石灘，水溢縱使歸海，水平留之入湖。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era, stone shoals were again piled up; when water overflowed it was allowed to return to the sea, and when the water level subsided it was retained to enter the lakes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing period, stone shoals were rebuilt so that when floods came, excess water could reach the sea, and when levels dropped, water was held back to feed the lakes.

sentences.zh: 歲久頹廢，萬一汶水北注，挾湖泉盡歸大清河，四百餘裡運道所關非小。

translations.literal: After many years these fell into ruin; if by chance the Wen should pour north, carrying lake and spring waters entirely into the Daqing River, the transport route of more than four hundred li would be gravely affected.
