translations.idiomatic: After years of neglect they had fallen into ruin. If the Wen River ever turned north and swept lake and spring waters into the Daqing River, more than four hundred li of canal would be at serious risk.

sentences.zh: 請飭總河相度形勢，修復舊石灘，改建滾水石壩，以為蓄洩。」

translations.literal: I request that the director-general of rivers survey the terrain, restore the old stone shoals, and rebuild them as rolling spillway stone dams for storage and release.
translations.idiomatic: I ask the director-general of rivers to survey the terrain, restore the old stone shoals, and rebuild them as rolling spillway dams for storage and discharge.

sentences.zh: 上命內閣學士何國宗等攜儀器輿圖，會總河齊蘇勒、巡撫陳世倌履勘，請如廷錫奏。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Grand Secretary He Guozong and others to carry instruments and cartographic charts, join Director-General Qisuole and Governor Chen Shirui in on-site inspection, and requested action as Tingxi had memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Grand Secretary He Guozong and others to bring instruments and maps and conduct an on-site survey with Director-General Qisuole and Governor Chen Shirui. They recommended adopting Jiang's proposals.

sentences.zh: 下九卿議行。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Nine Ministers for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the Nine Ministers for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷戶部尚書，充順天鄉試考官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to minister of revenue and served as examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1726 he was promoted to minister of revenue and appointed examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 既入闈，諭曰：「廷錫佐怡親王董理戶部諸事，秉公執正，胥吏嫉妒懷怨。

translations.literal: Once he had entered the examination compound, an edict stated: "Tingxi has assisted Prince Yi in overseeing affairs of the Ministry of Revenue, upholding fairness and rectitude; clerks and runners are jealous and harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered the examination hall, the emperor issued an edict: "Jiang Tingxi has assisted Prince Yi in managing Ministry of Revenue affairs with scrupulous fairness. Clerks and runners, jealous and resentful,

sentences.zh: 今廷錫典試，或乘此造作浮言，妄加謗議。

translations.literal: Now that Tingxi presides over the examination, some may seize this occasion to fabricate loose talk and recklessly slander him.
translations.idiomatic: may now seize on his role as examiner to spread rumors and slander him.

sentences.zh: 令步軍統領、順天府尹、五城御史察訪捕治。」

translations.literal: Let the metropolitan garrison commander, the Shuntian prefect, and the Five-City censors investigate, seek out offenders, and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan garrison commander, the Shuntian prefect, and the Five-City censors are ordered to investigate and arrest anyone responsible.

sentences.zh: 尋命兼領兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to hold concurrently the post of minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the concurrent post of minister of war.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，遣大臣奠茶酒，予其母封誥，發帑治喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died, the emperor sent a minister to offer libations of tea and wine, granted his mother a patent of ennoblement, and issued treasury funds for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the emperor sent a minister to offer libations, granted his mother a title of honor, and issued treasury funds for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 命廷錫奉母喪還裡，葬畢還京，在任守制。

translations.literal: Tingxi was ordered to return home to observe mourning for his mother; after burial he was to return to the capital and observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was ordered to return home for his mother's funeral, then come back to the capital and observe mourning without leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜文華殿大學士，仍兼領戶部，充聖祖實錄總裁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall, still concurrently heading the Ministry of Revenue, and made chief compiler of the Kangxi emperor's veritable records.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728 he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall while retaining the Ministry of Revenue and made chief compiler of the Kangxi emperor's veritable records.

sentences.zh: 七年，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given the additional rank of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1729 he was given the additional rank of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 命與果親王允禮總理三庫，予世職一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Prince Guo, Yunli, to administer jointly the Three Treasuries, and granted the hereditary rank of first-class adaha gushan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to administer the Three Treasuries jointly with Prince Guo, Yunli, and granted the hereditary rank of first-class adaha gushan.

sentences.zh: 九年，廷錫病，上遣醫療治。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Tingxi fell ill; the emperor sent physicians to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1731 Jiang fell ill, and the emperor sent physicians to treat him.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，病復作，上命日二次以病狀奏。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year his illness recurred; the emperor ordered reports on his condition twice daily.
translations.idiomatic: That summer his illness returned, and the emperor ordered twice-daily reports on his condition.

sentences.zh: 閏五月，卒，上為輟朝，遣大臣奠茶酒，賜祭葬，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month he died; the emperor suspended court for him, sent a minister to offer libations, granted sacrificial rites and funeral honors, and posthumously titled him Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month he died. The emperor suspended court, sent a minister to offer libations, granted state funeral honors, and gave him the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 廷錫工詩善畫，事聖祖內直二十餘年。

translations.literal: Tingxi was skilled at poetry and painting; he served Kangxi in inner attendance for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was accomplished in poetry and painting and served in the Kangxi emperor's inner service for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 世宗朝累遷擢，明練恪謹，被恩禮始終。

translations.literal: Under Shizong he was repeatedly promoted; keen and conscientious, he received favor and courtesy from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongzheng emperor he rose steadily through promotion—capable, conscientious, and favored with grace from first to last.

sentences.zh: 子溥，字質甫。

translations.literal: His son Pu, style name Zhifu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pu, whose style was Zhifu.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，賜舉人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng he was granted status as a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1729 he was granted status as a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 八年，進士，改庶吉士，直南書房，襲世職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he became a jinshi, was made a Hanlin bachelor, served in the Southern Study, and inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the palace examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, served in the Southern Study, and inherited the family hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 廷錫卒，溥奉喪歸，命葬畢即還京供職。

translations.literal: When Tingxi died, Pu returned home to observe the funeral; he was ordered to return to the capital and resume duty as soon as burial was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Tingxi died, Pu went home for the funeral and was ordered to return to the capital and resume duty as soon as the burial was complete.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1733 he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 四遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: After four promotions he reached grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he became a grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong he was appointed vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1740 he was appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「凡條奏發九卿會議，主稿衙門酌定準駁。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Whenever memorial proposals are sent to joint conference of the Nine Ministers, the drafting yamen determines approval or rejection.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Whenever a policy proposal is sent to joint conference among the Nine Ministers, the drafting ministry decides whether to approve or reject it.

sentences.zh: 會議日，書吏誦稿以待商度，其中原委曲折，一時難盡。

translations.literal: On the day of conference, clerks recite the draft awaiting discussion; the ins and outs and twists within cannot be fully grasped at once.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the conference, clerks read the draft aloud for discussion—but the full reasoning and complications cannot be absorbed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 請於會議前二日將議稿傳鈔，俾得詳勘暢言。

translations.literal: I request that two days before conference the draft for deliberation be circulated in copy, so that all may examine in detail and speak freely.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that copies of the draft be circulated two days before the conference so members can study it thoroughly and speak freely.

sentences.zh: 至命、盜案，刑部例不先定稿，俟議時平決；

translations.literal: As for homicide and robbery cases, the Ministry of Punishments by rule does not fix the draft beforehand but waits until conference to decide evenly;
translations.idiomatic: For homicide and robbery cases, the Ministry of Punishments does not prepare a draft in advance but leaves the decision to the conference;

sentences.zh: 不關命、盜各案，亦宜先期傳知，庶為審慎。」

translations.literal: Cases not involving homicide or robbery should likewise be communicated beforehand, that deliberation may be more careful.
translations.idiomatic: but for all other cases, advance circulation would still allow more careful deliberation.

sentences.zh: 下部議，如所請。

translations.literal: The proposal was sent down to the ministry for deliberation; action followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the ministry, which ruled as he had requested.

sentences.zh: 八年，授湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1743 he was appointed governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 九年，疏言：「永順及永綏、乾州、鳳凰諸處苗民貪暴之習未除，城步、綏寧尤多狡惡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he memorialized: "At Yongshun and at places such as Yongsui, Qianzhou, and Fenghuang, the Miao people's habits of greed and violence have not been eliminated; Chengbu and Suining especially have many cunning and wicked ones.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized: "Among the Miao at Yongshun and at Yongsui, Qianzhou, Fenghuang, and other posts, greedy and violent habits persist. Chengbu and Suining are especially rife with cunning offenders.

sentences.zh: 臣整飭武備，漸知守法。」

translations.literal: Your servant has put military readiness in order, and they are gradually learning to obey the law.
translations.idiomatic: I have tightened military discipline, and they are gradually learning to obey the law.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「馭苗以不擾為要，次則使知兵威不敢犯。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "In governing the Miao, non-disturbance is paramount; next is letting them know military might so they dare not transgress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "In governing the Miao, the key is to avoid undue harassment; next, let them feel the weight of military authority so they dare not offend.

sentences.zh: 此奏得之。」

translations.literal: This memorial hits the mark.
translations.idiomatic: This memorial states the matter well.

sentences.zh: 旋劾按察使明德不詳鞫盜案，奪官；

translations.literal: Soon afterward he impeached Provincial Judge Mingde for not thoroughly trying a robbery case and stripped him of office;
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Provincial Judge Mingde for failing to investigate a robbery case thoroughly and stripped him of office;

sentences.zh: 驛鹽道謝濟世老病，休致。

translations.literal: Postal and Salt Circuit Intendant Xie Jishi, being old and ill, was permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Postal and Salt Circuit Intendant Xie Jishi was permitted to retire on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡定奏請湖南濱湖荒土，勸民修築開墾，令溥察議。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Ding memorialized requesting that wasteland along Hunan's lakes be used to encourage the people to build dikes and open land for cultivation; Pu was ordered to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Ding proposed encouraging reclamation of wasteland along Hunan's lakes and ordered Pu to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 溥奏言：「近年湖濱淤地，築墾殆遍。

translations.literal: Pu memorialized: "In recent years silt land along the lakes has been almost entirely diked and reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Pu replied: "In recent years, lakeside silt lands have been almost entirely diked and reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 奔湍束為細流，洲渚悉加堵截，常有衝決之慮。

translations.literal: Rushing torrents are confined into slender streams; sandbars and islets are all blocked off; there is constant fear of breach and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Fast currents have been narrowed into trickles, and sandbars and islets blocked off—raising constant fears of breaches and floods.

sentences.zh: 沅江万子湖、湘陰文洲圍，士民請修築開墾。

translations.literal: At Wanzi Lake on the Yuan River and Wenzhou Enclosure in Xiangyin, gentry and commoners request dike-building and reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: At Wanzi Lake on the Yuan River and the Wenzhou Enclosure in Xiangyin, local residents have petitioned for dike-building and reclamation.

sentences.zh: 臣親往履勘，文洲圍倚山面江，四圍俱有舊堤，已議舉行。

translations.literal: Your servant personally went to inspect on site; Wenzhou Enclosure leans on mountains and faces the river, with old dikes on all four sides—it has already been decided to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: I inspected both sites in person. The Wenzhou Enclosure lies against hills facing the river and is already ringed by old dikes; work there has been approved.

sentences.zh: 萬子湖廣袤八十餘裡，四面受水，費大難築，並於上下游水利有礙。

translations.literal: Wanzi Lake is more than eighty li in breadth; it receives water on all four sides; the cost is great and building difficult, and it would also harm upstream and downstream water management.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzi Lake spans more than eighty li and receives water from every side. Diking would be costly and difficult and would harm water management up- and downstream.

sentences.zh: 臣以為湖地墾築已多，當防湖患，不可有意勸墾。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that lake land has already been largely reclaimed and diked; one should guard against lake disasters and must not deliberately encourage reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Enough lakeside land has already been reclaimed. We should guard against lake disasters rather than actively encourage further reclamation.

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor affirmed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his assessment.

sentences.zh: 十年，授吏部侍郎、軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed vice minister of personnel and assigned to duty in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1745 he was appointed vice minister of personnel with duty in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢戶部尚書，命專治部事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to minister of revenue and ordered to administer the ministry exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: In 1748 he was promoted to minister of revenue and ordered to devote himself solely to ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was given the additional rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1750 he was given the additional rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命協辦大學士，兼禮部尚書，掌翰林院事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was ordered to serve as assistant grand secretary, concurrently minister of rites, and director of Hanlin Academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1753 he was appointed assistant grand secretary while serving concurrently as minister of rites and director of Hanlin Academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，兼署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he concurrently acted as minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755 he was given acting charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授東閣大學士，兼領戶部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Dongge Hall and concurrently headed the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1759 he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Dongge Hall while retaining the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，溥病，上親臨視。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Pu fell ill; the emperor personally visited him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761, when Pu fell ill, the emperor visited him in person.

sentences.zh: 及卒，复親臨奠。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor again came in person to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the emperor again came in person to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，發帑治喪，賜祭葬，諡文恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the rank of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; treasury funds were issued for the funeral; sacrificial rites and funeral honors were granted; he was posthumously titled Wenk.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. Treasury funds were granted for his funeral, state funeral honors were bestowed, and he received the posthumous title Wenk.

sentences.zh: 子檙，進士。

translations.literal: His son Zhen was a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen passed the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 自編修累遷兵部侍郎；

translations.literal: From compiler he was promoted repeatedly until vice minister of war;
translations.idiomatic: Rising from compiler, he was promoted to vice minister of war;

sentences.zh: 賜棨，初授雲南楚雄知府，再至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Cici, at first appointed prefect of Chuxiong in Yunnan, later reached vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Cici was first appointed prefect of Chuxiong in Yunnan and later rose to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 並坐事奪官，左授光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Both were stripped of office for misconduct and demoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Both were dismissed for misconduct and demoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 复奪官，以世職守護裕陵。

translations.literal: Again stripped of office, they were assigned by hereditary rank to guard the Yuling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of office again, they were assigned to guard the Yuling Mausoleum under their hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 邁柱，喜塔拉氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Mai Zhu, of the Xitara clan, was a Bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mai Zhu, of the Xitara clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授筆帖式，三遷戶部員外郎，授御史。

translations.literal: At first appointed a clerk, he was promoted thrice to department director in the Ministry of Revenue and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk, rose through three promotions to department director in the Ministry of Revenue, and was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十五年，巡視福建鹽課。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of Kangxi he inspected Fujian salt levies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1716 he inspected Fujian salt levies.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，巡視寧古塔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he inspected Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: In 1723 he inspected Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 三年，命如荊州會將軍武納哈籍前任將軍阿魯家，償侵蝕兵餉。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered to go to Jingzhou to join General Wunaha in confiscating the property of former general Aru's family to repay embezzled military pay.
translations.idiomatic: In 1725 he was ordered to Jingzhou to join General Wunaha in seizing the property of former general Aru's family to repay embezzled military funds.

sentences.zh: 議荊州近縣民有原鬻地者，官購俾兵耕種，或招佃徵租，兵婚喪量佽之。

translations.literal: It was proposed that in counties near Jingzhou where people had formerly sold land, the government should purchase it for soldiers to farm, or recruit tenant farmers and collect rent, with measured advances for soldiers' weddings and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: It was proposed that where residents of counties near Jingzhou had previously sold land, the government should buy it back for soldiers to farm, or lease it out and collect rent, with modest advances for soldiers' weddings and funerals.

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The proposal was sent down to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 擢工部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice minister of works; transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of works and then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 命如江西按治德安知縣蕭彬、武寧知縣廖科齡虧帑，並命察通省錢糧積弊。

translations.literal: He was ordered to Jiangxi to investigate magistrates Xiao Bin of De'an and Liao Keling of Wuning for treasury deficits, and to examine accumulated abuses in provincial tax and grain collection.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Jiangxi to investigate magistrates Xiao Bin of De'an and Liao Keling of Wuning for treasury deficits and to examine accumulated abuses in provincial tax and grain collection.

sentences.zh: 尋命署巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to serve as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting governor.

sentences.zh: 疏請以江西額徵丁銀攤入地糧，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that Jiangxi's assessed poll-tax silver be merged into land-tax grain collection; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting that Jiangxi's poll tax be folded into the land tax, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，授湖廣總督，命俟江西事畢赴任。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed governor-general of Huguang and ordered to take up the post after Jiangxi affairs were complete.
translations.idiomatic: In 1727 he was appointed governor-general of Huguang and ordered to take up the post once his Jiangxi duties were finished.

sentences.zh: 邁柱疏陳：「江西倉穀虧缺，弊在無穀無銀，虛報存貯，及至交代，又虛報民間借領，後任徵追，悉歸無著。

translations.literal: Mai Zhu memorialized: "Jiangxi granary grain is deficient; the abuse lies in having neither grain nor silver yet falsely reporting stocks on hand, and when turnover comes, again falsely reporting that the populace borrowed and received it—successors then collect and pursue payment, all to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: Mai Zhu memorialized: "Jiangxi's granary stocks are deficient. The abuse is that officials report grain on hand when there is neither grain nor silver, and at turnover falsely claim the grain was lent to the populace—leaving successors to collect debts that can never be recovered.

sentences.zh: 又或出糶倉穀得價侵用，及至交代，以二錢一石折價，後任不敷糴補。

translations.literal: Or else granary grain is sold off and the proceeds embezzled; when turnover comes, it is reckoned at two cash per shi, and successors cannot afford to buy grain to make up the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Or granary grain is sold off and the proceeds embezzled; at turnover the deficit is reckoned at two cash per shi, leaving successors unable to afford the grain needed to make up the loss.

sentences.zh: 又或因不敷之故，並此折價而亦侵用，及至交代，復稱民欠，多方掩飾。

translations.literal: Again, because funds were insufficient, even this converted valuation was likewise embezzled; when the handover came, they again claimed it as arrears owed by the people and concealed it by every possible means.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, when funds still fell short, officials would embezzle even this discounted valuation; at turnover they would relabel the deficit as tax arrears owed by the people and conceal it by every dodge available.

sentences.zh: 皆因前任巡撫裴幰度，布政使陳安策、張楷徇庇所誤。」

translations.literal: All were due to the misleading shielding by the former governor Pei Xiandu and the provincial commissioners Chen Ance and Zhang Kai.
translations.idiomatic: All this stemmed from the misleading protection offered by the former governor Pei Xiandu and the provincial commissioners Chen Ance and Zhang Kai.

sentences.zh: 上為奪幰度等官，察究追完。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon removed Xiandu and the others from office and ordered investigation and full recovery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Xiandu and his colleagues of their offices and ordered a thorough inquiry to recover the full amount.

sentences.zh: 又言：「江西通省公用需款，請視河南、湖廣諸省例，提州、縣耗羨二分充用，另提充各員養廉，多至一分五釐，少至四釐，餘仍留州縣養贍。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "For Jiangxi's province-wide public expenses, I ask that we follow the precedent of Henan, Huguang, and other provinces: draw two fen of prefectural and county surplus fees for use, and separately draw amounts for each official's integrity stipend—up to one fen five li at most and four li at least—while the remainder still goes to prefectures and counties for local upkeep.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he proposed that Jiangxi's province-wide public expenses follow the Henan and Huguang model: allocate two fen of prefectural and county surplus fees, set aside separate integrity stipends for officials ranging from four li to one fen five li, and leave the rest with prefectures and counties for local upkeep.

sentences.zh: 巡撫及司道，亦於所提一分五釐內量行支用。」

translations.literal: The governor and circuit intendants also drew as needed from the allocated one fen five li."
translations.idiomatic: The governor and circuit intendants were also authorized to draw from that one fen five li allocation as needed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「江西被災州縣，設廠煮賑，米價石至一兩三四錢。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "In Jiangxi's disaster-stricken prefectures and counties, relief kitchens were established for porridge distribution, and rice prices reached one tael and three or four cash per shi.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that in Jiangxi's disaster counties, relief kitchens had been opened and rice had risen to one tael three or four cash per shi.

sentences.zh: 請於未被災州縣發銀預購平糶。」

translations.literal: He requested that silver be issued from undamaged prefectures and counties to pre-purchase grain for fair-price sale."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that silver be sent from unaffected counties to buy grain in advance and sell it at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 又言：「南安、贛州，閩、廣交界，及鄱陽湖濱，最易藏奸。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "Nan'an and Ganzhou, on the Fujian–Guangdong border, and the shores of Poyang Lake are the easiest places for wrongdoers to hide.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned that Nan'an and Ganzhou on the Fujian–Guangdong border and the shores of Poyang Lake were prime havens for criminals.

sentences.zh: 萬載、寧州等地，棚民聚集，素好多事。

translations.literal: In places such as Wanzai and Ningzhou, shed-dwellers gathered and had long been prone to making trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanzai, Ningzhou, and similar districts, clusters of shed-dwellers had a longstanding reputation for unrest.

sentences.zh: 已飭嚴整塘汛，操練標兵，豫為之備。」

translations.literal: He had already ordered patrol posts strictly reorganized, garrison troops drilled, and preparations made in advance."
translations.idiomatic: He had already tightened patrol posts, drilled the garrison troops, and made advance preparations.

sentences.zh: 得旨，嘉其條畫詳晰，令新任巡撫照行。

translations.literal: Receiving the imperial rescript, the throne praised the clarity of his provisions and ordered the incoming governor to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the memorial's thorough provisions and instructed the new governor to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 尋讞定彬等俱論斬。

translations.literal: Soon the verdict was settled: Bin and the others were all sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the cases were decided and Bin and his accomplices were all sentenced to execution.

sentences.zh: 並請令徇庇之上官分償虧帑，上命自雍正六年起著為例。

translations.literal: He also requested that the superiors who had shielded them be ordered to share repayment of the treasury deficit; the emperor commanded that this be established as precedent from the sixth year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that shielding superiors be made to share the burden of repaying the treasury deficit; the emperor made this rule permanent from the sixth year of Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 獎邁柱秉公持正，下部議敘，乃赴湖廣任。

translations.literal: Mai Zhu was rewarded for acting impartially and uprightly; the ministry was ordered to deliberate commendation, and then he took up his post in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Mai Zhu was commended for his impartial integrity, the ministry was instructed to record his merit, and he then proceeded to his post in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 湖廣瀕江州縣頻年被水，邁柱令民間按糧派夫，修築江堤，議定確估土方夫數及加修尺寸，並歲修搶險諸例。

translations.literal: In Huguang's riverside prefectures and counties, floods struck year after year; Mai Zhu had the populace apportioned corvée labor by grain-tax quota to repair river dikes, establishing fixed estimates for earthwork laborers and dimensions for supplementary repairs, as well as rules for annual maintenance and emergency repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang's riverside counties suffered flooding year after year; Mai Zhu assigned corvée according to grain-tax quotas to repair the river dikes, setting fixed standards for earthwork crews, supplementary dimensions, and rules for annual upkeep and emergency repairs.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，上發帑六萬，命視工多寡分給。

translations.literal: When his memorial reached the throne, the emperor disbursed sixty thousand taels from the treasury and ordered distribution according to the scale of the works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan, released sixty thousand taels from the treasury, and ordered that the funds be divided according to the scale of each project.

sentences.zh: 鎮筸苗最悍，屢入內地剽掠。

translations.literal: The Miao of Zhenqian were the fiercest and repeatedly entered the interior to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenqian Miao were the fiercest and raided the interior again and again.

sentences.zh: 邁柱疏言：「臣聞雲南提督張國正先任鎮筸總兵，以雕剿法治苗。

translations.literal: Mai Zhu submitted a memorial: "Your minister has heard that Yunnan provincial commander Zhang Guozheng, when he previously served as Zhenqian brigade commander, governed the Miao with the 'eagle pursuit' method.
translations.idiomatic: Mai Zhu reported: "I have heard that when Zhang Guozheng of Yunnan was brigade commander at Zhenqian, he pacified the Miao with a tactic called 'eagle pursuit.

sentences.zh: 聞有警，诇為何種苗，所屬何寨，即攜兵馳往，圍寨搜擒。

translations.literal: Upon hearing an alarm, he reconnoitered what kind of Miao they were and which stockade they belonged to, then immediately led troops in rapid march, surrounded the stockade, and searched to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: At the first alarm he would identify the Miao band and its stockade, then ride out at once, surround the settlement, and hunt down the culprits.

sentences.zh: 如雕之捕鳥，取其速而鳥可必得。

translations.literal: It was like an eagle catching a bird: relying on speed, the bird could be surely seized.
translations.idiomatic: Like an eagle seizing its prey, speed ensured the quarry could not escape.

sentences.zh: 臣今與總兵週一德循行此法，但期得罪人而止，不敢多為殺戮。」

translations.literal: Your minister now follows this method together with brigade commander Zhou Yide, only aiming to stop at those who have committed offenses, and not daring to slaughter excessively."
translations.idiomatic: I now apply the same method with Brigadier Zhou Yide, seeking only to apprehend the guilty and refusing to indulge in wholesale slaughter."

sentences.zh: 居數年，又疏言：「收繳六里鎮筸土司所藏鳥槍，完整者俾兵充用，餘改造農具，給土苗耕作。

translations.literal: After several years, he submitted another memorial: "Collect the bird guns hoarded by the native chieftains of Liuzhen in Zhenqian; intact ones shall be issued to the troops for use, and the rest remade into farming tools and given to the indigenous Miao for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he proposed confiscating bird guns stockpiled by the Liuzhen Zhenqian chieftains—serviceable pieces would arm the troops, and the rest would be converted into farm tools for Miao farmers.

sentences.zh: 土苗所用環刀、標槍，亦令給價收繳。」

translations.literal: The ring knives and javelins used by the indigenous Miao were likewise to be bought back and collected at set prices."
translations.idiomatic: Ring knives and javelins held by the Miao were likewise to be bought back at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「所奏深得賣刀買犢之意。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "What you have memorialized deeply captures the meaning of 'selling one's knife to buy an ox calf.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Your proposal captures perfectly the spirit of disarming men and putting them to the plow.

sentences.zh: 環刀、標槍，自當收繳，可順其原，不宜強迫​​。」

translations.literal: Ring knives and javelins should indeed be collected, but this may follow their original inclination and ought not be forced."
translations.idiomatic: Ring knives and javelins should be collected, but persuade rather than coerce."

sentences.zh: 疏定苗與民為市，於分界地設市，一月以三日為期，不得越界出入。

translations.literal: His memorial established markets where Miao and commoners traded: markets were set at the boundary, with three days each month as the period, and crossing the boundary to enter or leave was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: He regulated trade between Miao and Han by opening border markets three days a month and forbidding either side to cross the boundary.

sentences.zh: 民以物往市，預報地方官，知會塘汛查驗。

translations.literal: When commoners brought goods to market, they were to report in advance to the local officials, who would notify the patrol posts to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners had to notify local officials before bringing goods to market, and patrol posts would inspect the shipments.

sentences.zh: 苗疆州縣立苗長，選良苗充​​民壯，備差遣訪緝。

translations.literal: In Miao-frontier prefectures and counties, Miao headmen were established; good Miao were selected to serve as local militia for dispatch on searches and arrests.
translations.idiomatic: Miao counties appointed Miao headmen and enrolled trustworthy Miao as local militia for patrols and arrests.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰督雲、貴，建策改土歸流，邁柱亦行之湖廣，收永順、保靖、桑植三土司。

translations.literal: Ortai supervised Yunnan and Guizhou and proposed the policy of replacing native chieftain rule with direct administration; Mai Zhu also carried this out in Huguang, bringing under direct rule the three chieftains of Yongshun, Baojing, and Sangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: While Ortai was implementing direct administration in Yunnan and Guizhou, Mai Zhu extended the same policy in Huguang, abolishing the Yongshun, Baojing, and Sangzhi chieftaincies.

sentences.zh: 永順設府縣，仍其名，又於府西北設縣曰龍山。

translations.literal: For Yongshun, a prefecture and county were established under the original name; northwest of the prefectural seat a new county called Longshan was also established.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshun became a prefecture and county under its old name, and a new county, Longshan, was created northwest of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 保靖、桑植各設縣，仍其名。

translations.literal: Baojing and Sangzhi each had a county established, retaining their original names.
translations.idiomatic: Baojing and Sangzhi were each organized as counties under their former names.

sentences.zh: 收容美土司設州，曰鶴峰，所屬五峰新設縣曰長樂。

translations.literal: The annexed Rongmei chieftain's territory was made into a prefecture called Hefeng; its subordinate Wufeng was newly established as the county of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: The annexed Rongmei chieftaincy became Hefeng Prefecture, with its former Wufeng domain reorganized as Changle County.

sentences.zh: 並改彝陵州為府，曰宜昌，領新設州縣。

translations.literal: Yiling Prefecture was also changed into a prefecture called Yichang, which governed the newly established prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yiling Prefecture was upgraded to Yichang Prefecture, which oversaw the newly created counties and sub-prefectures.

sentences.zh: 收第岡土司，改永定衛為縣，以其地屬焉。

translations.literal: The Digang chieftain was brought under direct rule; Yongding Guard was changed into a county and its territory was placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: After absorbing the Digang chieftaincy, Yongding Guard was converted into a county and its former domain incorporated.

sentences.zh: 上命通察湖廣積欠錢糧，都計銀三十餘萬，令與巡撫馬會伯、王國棟同董其事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a comprehensive investigation of accumulated tax and grain arrears in Huguang, totaling more than three hundred thousand taels of silver, and directed him to supervise the matter jointly with governors Ma Huibo and Wang Guodong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a province-wide audit of Huguang's tax arrears, which totaled more than three hundred thousand taels, and put Mai Zhu in charge alongside Governors Ma Huibo and Wang Guodong.

sentences.zh: 逾年，報湖南已完六萬有奇，湖北已完八萬有奇。

translations.literal: After more than a year, it was reported that Hunan had recovered a little over sixty thousand, and Hubei a little over eighty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Hunan had recovered a little over sixty thousand taels and Hubei a little over eighty thousand.

sentences.zh: 尋察出沔陽積欠內為官侵役蝕包攬未完者三萬有奇，其實欠在民者三萬二千有奇。

translations.literal: It was soon discovered that of Mianyang's accumulated arrears, a little over thirty thousand remained unrecovered owing to official embezzlement, corvée abuses, and tax-farming; the amount actually owed by the people was a little over thirty-two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The audit revealed that of Mianyang's backlog, more than thirty thousand taels remained uncollected because officials had embezzled, extorted, or farmed the taxes, while genuine arrears owed by commoners came to a little over thirty-two thousand.

sentences.zh: 上以沔陽常被水，民欠命予豁除。

translations.literal: Because Mianyang was frequently inundated, the emperor ordered that the people's arrears be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Mianyang suffered chronic flooding, the emperor ordered the people's arrears forgiven.

sentences.zh: 七年，邁柱疏請以湖廣額徵丁銀攤入地糧，從之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Mai Zhu submitted a memorial requesting that Huguang's quota poll-tax silver be assessed into the land tax; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Mai Zhu proposed merging Huguang's poll tax into the land tax assessment, and the throne assented.

sentences.zh: 邁柱督湖廣數年，聲績顯著。

translations.literal: Mai Zhu supervised Huguang for several years, and his reputation and achievements were conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: After several years governing Huguang, Mai Zhu's reputation and record stood out.

sentences.zh: 他所區畫，如以漢陽通判移漢口，荊州通判移沙市。

translations.literal: Among his other arrangements were such measures as transferring the Hanyang sub-prefect to Hankou and the Jingzhou sub-prefect to Shashi.
translations.idiomatic: His other reforms included relocating the Hanyang sub-prefect to Hankou and the Jingzhou sub-prefect to Shashi.

sentences.zh: 又裁施州、大田二衛所，合為縣曰恩施，復請改為府，曰施南，設縣四，曰宣恩、來鳳、咸豐、利川。

translations.literal: He also abolished the two guard posts of Shizhou and Datian, merged them into a county called Enshi, then requested that it be changed into a prefecture called Shinan, with four counties established: Xuan'en, Laifeng, Xianfeng, and Lichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the Shizhou and Datian guard posts and merged them into Enshi County, then persuaded the court to elevate the region to Shinan Prefecture with four new counties: Xuan'en, Laifeng, Xianfeng, and Lichuan.

sentences.zh: 宜昌既為府，設附郭縣曰東湖，又以歸州及所領長陽、興山、巴東諸縣隸焉。

translations.literal: Once Yichang became a prefecture, an attached county called Donghu was established, and Guizhou together with its subordinate counties Changyang, Xingshan, and Badong were placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: With Yichang elevated to a prefecture, he created Donghu County at the seat and placed Guizhou and its counties Changyang, Xingshan, and Badong under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 道州及寧遠、永明、江華諸縣鄰廣西，請以永州同知移江華，並分設游擊、守備，調駐兵千五百，與廣西桂臨營月三次會哨。

translations.literal: Daozhou and the counties of Ningyuan, Yongming, and Jianghua border Guangxi; he requested that the Yongzhou sub-prefect be moved to Jianghua, that separate brigade and garrison commanders be established, that fifteen hundred troops be transferred and stationed, and that joint patrols be held three times a month with Guangxi's Guilin garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Because Daozhou and the counties of Ningyuan, Yongming, and Jianghua adjoin Guangxi, he moved the Yongzhou sub-prefect to Jianghua, posted brigade and garrison commanders with fifteen hundred troops, and arranged thrice-monthly joint patrols with Guangxi's Guilin garrison.

sentences.zh: 永順、保靖、桑植三營新立，月餉給米折，永順石折一兩，保靖、桑植石折八錢，以苗疆米貴，不與他營同。

translations.literal: The three newly established garrisons of Yongshun, Baojing, and Sangzhi received monthly grain stipends paid as cash equivalents: Yongshun at one tael per shi, Baojing and Sangzhi at eight cash per shi, because grain was dear in the Miao frontier and their rates differed from other garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: For the new Yongshun, Baojing, and Sangzhi garrisons he set cash equivalents for grain rations—one tael per shi at Yongshun, eight cash at Baojing and Sangzhi—reflecting the higher rice prices on the Miao frontier.

sentences.zh: 上悉如所請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all according to his requests.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted every request.

sentences.zh: 十三年，召拜武英殿大學士，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was summoned and appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, concurrently serving as minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was recalled to court as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory and concurrent minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，兼管工部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he also supervised the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he took charge of the Ministry of Works as well.

sentences.zh: 二年，以病乞解任。

translations.literal: In the second year, on grounds of illness he requested release from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he asked to retire on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，賜祭葬，諡文恭。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; funeral sacrifices were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year; the court granted him state funeral honors and the posthumous title Wengong, "Cultured and Reverent."

sentences.zh: 同時督撫入為大學士者，又有白潢、趙國麟。

translations.literal: Among the governors and governor-generals who at the same time entered the capital as grand secretaries were also Bai Huang and Zhao Guolin.
translations.idiomatic: Other governors elevated to grand secretary at the same time included Bai Huang and Zhao Guolin.

sentences.zh: 潢，字近微，漢軍鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Huang, whose style was Jinwei, was a Han bondsman of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, courtesy name Jinwei, was a Han bondsman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授筆帖式，考授內閣中書，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a clerk, then through examination appointed a Hanlin drafter, and was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerical secretary, passed the examination for Hanlin drafter, and rose to reader.

sentences.zh: 授福建糧驛道僉事，以父憂去官。

translations.literal: He was appointed an assistant intendant of the Fujian grain-and-post circuit, and left office upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as an assistant intendant on Fujian's grain-and-post circuit, then resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除山東登萊青道僉事，遷貴州貴東道參議。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed assistant intendant of the Shandong Deng-Lai-Qing circuit and was later promoted to vice intendant of the Guizhou Guidong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as assistant intendant on Shandong's Deng-Lai-Qing circuit and was promoted to vice intendant of Guizhou's Guidong circuit.

sentences.zh: 以巡撫劉廕樞薦，就遷按察使。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Governor Liu Yinshu, he was promoted directly to provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Governor Liu Yinshu, he was promoted straight to provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 潢操守廉潔，聞於聖祖，擢湖南布政使。

translations.literal: Huang's integrity and clean conduct were known to the Kangxi Emperor, and he was promoted to Hunan provincial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His upright, incorruptible service reached the Kangxi Emperor, who promoted him to Hunan provincial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未上官，會廕樞以請緩西師，命詣軍前察視，潢護貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: Before he took up his new post, Yinshu requested a slowing of the western campaign and was ordered to the army front for inspection; Huang acted as governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his Hunan post, Yinshu petitioned to slow the western campaign and was sent to inspect the front; Huang served as acting governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 貴州山多田少，諸鎮營兵餉米，於徵米諸州縣支發。

translations.literal: Guizhou had many mountains and few fields; grain rations for the various garrison troops were issued in the prefectures and counties that collected grain in kind.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou's rugged terrain left little farmland, so garrison grain rations were issued through the counties that collected rice taxes.

sentences.zh: 以運道艱阻，改徵折色，遲至次年春夏，米值昂不足以糴。

translations.literal: Because the transport routes were arduous, collection was changed to cash payment; by the following spring or summer, when prices were high, the cash was insufficient to purchase grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hazardous transport routes had led to cash commutation, but by the following spring and summer rice prices had risen so high that the cash could no longer buy enough grain.

sentences.zh: 諸驛例設夫百、馬四十五，而巡撫以下私函付驛，謂之便牌，役夫至數百。

translations.literal: Post stations were by regulation allotted one hundred bearers and forty-five horses, but officials from the governor downward sent private letters through the posts—called "convenience tokens"—and requisitioned as many as several hundred bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Post stations were allotted a hundred bearers and forty-five horses by regulation, yet officials down to the governor used private "convenience tokens" that could press hundreds of bearers into service.

sentences.zh: 潢奏請兵米於籓庫借支，州縣徵解歸項，並檄諸驛禁便牌。

translations.literal: Huang memorialized requesting that army grain be advanced on loan from the provincial treasury and repaid when the prefectures and counties collected and remitted the funds, and also issued orders to all post stations forbidding convenience tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Huang arranged advances from the provincial treasury for troop grain, with counties responsible for repayment, and banned the convenience tokens at every post station.

sentences.zh: 兵民困皆蘇。

translations.literal: The hardships of both soldiers and commoners were all relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Both soldiers and commoners soon felt the relief.

sentences.zh: 又以貴州僻遠，官於外，商於外，皆不肯歸，潢奏請勒限回籍。

translations.literal: Because Guizhou was remote, officials and merchants who went elsewhere were unwilling to return; Huang memorialized requesting enforced deadlines for returning to their registered domiciles.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guizhou was remote, officials and merchants who left the province seldom returned; Huang ordered them home under strict deadlines.

sentences.zh: 貴州民初以為不便，久之文物漸盛，乃思潢惠焉。

translations.literal: The people of Guizhou at first regarded this as inconvenient, but in time culture and accomplishments gradually flourished, and they came to appreciate Huang's beneficence.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou elites initially resented the policy, but as learning and culture flourished they came to credit Huang's foresight.

sentences.zh: 廕樞還貴州，調潢江西。

translations.literal: When Yinshu returned to Guizhou, Huang was transferred to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinshu returned to Guizhou, Huang was moved to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 入覲，至熱河謁上，即擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: On presenting himself at audience, when he reached Rehe and had an audience with the emperor, he was immediately promoted to governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: During his audience tour he met the emperor at Rehe and was immediately appointed governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 潢革諸州縣漕節陋例，並令火耗限加一，舊加至三四者，悉罷除之，不率者奏劾。

translations.literal: Huang abolished shabby customary practices in grain transport at the prefectures and counties, and ordered that surcharges on meltage fees be limited to one part; old additions reaching three or four parts were all abolished, and those who did not comply were impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Huang swept away abusive grain-transport customs and capped meltage surcharges at ten percent, abolishing older levies that had reached thirty or forty percent and impeaching officials who resisted.

sentences.zh: 湖口關地險港窄，潢度關右武曲港山勢開闊，可容千艘，乃濬江口，建草壩，使估舟得聚泊。

translations.literal: The Hukou Pass had perilous terrain and a narrow harbor; Huang surveyed Wuju Harbor to the right of the pass, where the mountain slopes opened wide enough to accommodate a thousand vessels, then dredged the river mouth and built a grassy embankment so merchant boats could gather and moor.
translations.idiomatic: Hukou Pass was treacherous and its harbor cramped; Huang identified Wuju Harbor on the right as broad enough for a thousand vessels, dredged the river mouth, built a temporary embankment, and gave merchant shipping a safe anchorage.

sentences.zh: 建亭頌潢德。

translations.literal: A pavilion was built praising Huang's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people erected a pavilion in his honor.

sentences.zh: 會城西南有袁、贛二江，至臨江合流，舊有堤久圮，春夏水發，往往壞田廬。

translations.literal: Southwest of the provincial capital were the Yuan and Gan rivers, which joined at Linjiang; an old dike there had long been ruined, and when waters rose in spring and summer they often destroyed fields and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the provincial seat the Yuan and Gan rivers meet at Linjiang; an ancient dike there had collapsed, and spring floods routinely ruined fields and homes.

sentences.zh: 潢奏請重建，九閱月而成。

translations.literal: Huang memorialized requesting reconstruction, and it was completed after nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Huang rebuilt the dike, finishing the work in nine months.

sentences.zh: 民自是無水患，號為白公堤。

translations.literal: From then on the people had no flood disasters, and they called it Prefect Bai's Dike.
translations.idiomatic: The people thereafter lived free of floods and named the structure Prefect Bai's Dike.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，奏請補京職，授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, he memorialized requesting a capital appointment and was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he sought a capital posting and was appointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，命協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, when the Yongzheng Emperor ascended the throne, he was ordered to assist as grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzheng took the throne in the sixty-first year, Huang was appointed acting grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋授文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Splendor.

sentences.zh: 疏辭，不許。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial declining; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to decline but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 充聖祖實錄總裁。

translations.literal: He served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Kangxi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief editor of the Kangxi Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，以疾乞解任，許之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, on grounds of illness he requested release from office; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongzheng he retired on account of illness, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 潢撫江西時，南昌、吉安、撫州、饒州四府舊有落地稅千三百兩有奇，設大使徵收。

translations.literal: When Huang governed Jiangxi, the four prefectures of Nanchang, Ji'an, Fuzhou, and Raozhou had long levied a landing tax of a little over thirteen hundred taels, collected by specially appointed agents.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Jiangxi, Huang found that Nanchang, Ji'an, Fuzhou, and Raozhou had levied a landing tax of more than thirteen hundred taels through specially appointed collectors.

sentences.zh: 潢以官役苛徵​​，令停收。

translations.literal: Because official runners collected it harshly, Huang ordered collection stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the levies extracted harshly by official runners, he halted collection.

sentences.zh: 巡撫、司道公捐代納，偽編納稅人名冊報部，王企崝、裴幰度代為巡撫，皆如潢例。

translations.literal: The governor and circuit intendants paid from their own donations in substitution, falsely compiled rosters of taxpayers for reporting to the ministry; Wang Qisong and Pei Xiandu, while acting as governor, all followed Huang's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He and his colleagues paid the tax from their own pockets and filed fabricated taxpayer rosters with the ministry; his successors Wang Qisong and Pei Xiandu did the same.

sentences.zh: 及汪漋至，以其事聞，且請裁大使。

translations.literal: When Wang Yong arrived, he reported the matter and also requested abolition of the special collectors.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yong took office he reported the arrangement and asked to abolish the special collectors.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「國家經制錢糧，豈可意為增減？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The state's fixed revenue in taxes and grain—how can it be increased or decreased at will?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor objected: "How can fixed state revenues be altered on a whim?

sentences.zh: 若此稅不當收，潢當請豁免，何得以公捐代完，沽名邀譽？」

translations.literal: If this tax ought not to be collected, Huang should have requested exemption—why finish payment through officials' donations to burnish his reputation?"
translations.idiomatic: If the tax was improper Huang should have sought exemption—not quietly paid it out of pocket to burnish his name."

sentences.zh: 下部議，奪潢官。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation, and Huang was stripped of his office.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the ministry, which stripped Huang of rank.

sentences.zh: 漋亦坐左遷，稅如舊例徵收。

translations.literal: Yong was also punished with demotion, and the tax was collected according to the old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong was demoted as well, and the tax was restored to its former levy.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，潢卒，命還大學士銜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, Huang died; he was ordered posthumously restored to grand secretary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Huang died in the second year of Qianlong, and the throne restored his grand secretary rank posthumously.

sentences.zh: 國麟，字仁圃，山東泰安人。

translations.literal: Guolin, whose style was Renpu, was a native of Tai'an in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin, courtesy name Renpu, came from Tai'an in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 祖瑗，手書春秋內外傳，史、漢蒙文授之。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuan personally copied the Spring and Autumn Annals with its Inner and Outer Traditions and the Mongol-script texts of the Records and the Han, and taught them to him.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuan tutored him from hand-copied editions of the Spring and Autumn Annals and Mongol-script versions of the Records and Han.

sentences.zh: 篤志於學，以程、硃為宗。

translations.literal: He was devoted in will to learning and took the Cheng–Zhu school as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued learning with single-minded devotion in the Cheng–Zhu Neo-Confucian tradition.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，授直隸長垣知縣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he was appointed magistrate of Changyuan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he was posted as magistrate of Changyuan in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 當官清峻，以禮導民，民戴如父母。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and stern; he guided the people through ritual, and the people honored him as they would parents.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with austere integrity and led the people through ritual decorum; they revered him as they would their own parents.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞其賢，雍正二年，擢永平知府。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor heard of his worth and in the second year of Yongzheng promoted him to prefect of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of his reputation, Yongzheng promoted him to prefect of Yongping in the second year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 三遷福建布政使，調河南。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Fujian provincial commissioner and was transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through three postings to become Fujian provincial commissioner, then was transferred to Henan.

sentences.zh: 擢福建巡撫，調安徽。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of Fujian and transferred to Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Fujian and soon moved to Anhui.

sentences.zh: 御史蔣炳奏請州縣徵收錢糧，依部頒定額，刊印由單，申布政使覈發。

translations.literal: Censor Jiang Bing memorialized that when prefectures and counties collected taxes and grain, they should follow the ministry's issued quotas, print and issue tax receipts, and apply to the provincial commissioner for examination and issuance.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jiang Bing proposed that counties collect taxes according to ministry quotas, print standardized receipt forms, and submit them to provincial commissioners for approval.

sentences.zh: 國麟以安徽通省數百萬由單由司覈發，恐誤徵收，疏請停止。

translations.literal: Guolin, considering that Anhui's province-wide millions of tax receipts would be examined and issued by the provincial administration, feared errors in collection and memorialized requesting that the plan be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin argued that routing millions of Anhui tax receipts through the provincial administration would invite collection errors, and he memorialized to stop the scheme.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士方苞疏言：「常平倉穀原定每年存七糶三，南省地卑濕，應令因地制宜。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Fang Bao memorialized: "The ever-normal granary grain was originally fixed at keeping seven parts and selling three each year; the southern provinces have low, damp ground and should be allowed to adapt measures to local conditions."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Fang Bao argued that the standard rule—retaining seventy percent of ever-normal granary grain and releasing thirty percent each year—should be relaxed in the damp lowlands of the south, where local conditions demanded flexibility.

sentences.zh: 下督撫詳覈。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the governors-general and governors for detailed examination.
translations.idiomatic: The throne referred the proposal to provincial governors for review.

sentences.zh: 國麟疏言：「安徽所屬州縣濱江湖者，當改糶半存半，他州縣仍循舊例。」

translations.literal: Guolin memorialized: "Among the prefectures and counties under Anhui that border rivers and lakes, half should be sold and half stored; other prefectures and counties should still follow the old precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Guolin proposed that Anhui counties on rivers and lakes switch to a fifty-fifty store-and-sell ratio, while the rest of the province keep the old rule.

sentences.zh: 並下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was also referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials went to the ministry for deliberation and enactment.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，擢刑部尚書，調禮部，兼領國子監。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was promoted to Minister of Punishments, transferred to the Ministry of Rites, and concurrently directed the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong he became Minister of Punishments, moved to the Ministry of Rites, and took charge of the Imperial Academy as well.

sentences.zh: 四年，授文華殿大學士，兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, concurrently serving as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered the Grand Secretariat as Wenhua Hall Grand Secretary while retaining the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，御史仲永檀疏劾內閣學士許王猷邀九卿至京師民俞長庚家弔喪，國麟亦親往，下王大臣勘不實。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Censor Zhong Yongtan memorialized impeaching Grand Secretary Xu Wangyou for inviting the Nine Ministers to a commoner Yu Changgeng's home in the capital to mourn; Guolin also went in person. The case was referred to princes and grand ministers for investigation and found untrue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Censor Zhong Yongtan accused Grand Secretary Xu Wangyou of summoning the Nine Ministers to mourn at a commoner's house in the capital; Guolin had attended as well. An inquiry by princes and senior ministers found the charge baseless.

sentences.zh: 國麟乞引退，上留之。

translations.literal: Guolin begged to withdraw, but the emperor kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin offered to retire, but the emperor refused to release him.

sentences.zh: 俄，給事中盧秉純复論國麟當上舉永檀疏面詰，陽若不知，出告其戚光祿寺卿劉籓長，籓長被命休致；

translations.literal: Soon afterward, Supervising Secretary Lu Bingchun again argued that when the emperor raised Yongtan's memorial to question Guolin to his face, Guolin feigned ignorance; afterward he told his kinsman Liu Fanzhang, Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, who was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Supervising Secretary Lu Bingchun charged that when the emperor confronted Guolin with Yongtan's memorial, Guolin had pretended ignorance, then confided the matter to his kinsman Liu Fanzhang of the Court of Imperial Entertainments—who was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 國麟又告以為侍郎蔣炳所劾。

translations.literal: Guolin also said he had been impeached by Vice Minister Jiang Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin further claimed that Vice Minister Jiang Bing had impeached him.

sentences.zh: 上命大學士鄂爾泰、張廷玉召國麟及籓長相質，籓長力辯。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Grand Secretaries Ortai and Zhang Tingyu to summon Guolin and Fanzhang to confront each other; Fanzhang vigorously defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Grand Secretaries Ortai and Zhang Tingyu summon both men for a face-to-face hearing; Fanzhang stoutly denied the accusation.

sentences.zh: 上命毋深究，令鄂爾泰、張廷玉諭國麟引退。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that the matter not be pursued further and directed Ortai and Zhang Tingyu to instruct Guolin to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declined to press the case further and told Ortai and Zhang Tingyu to advise Guolin to retire.

sentences.zh: 國麟疏未即上，上降詔詰責，左授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Guolin did not promptly submit his memorial of withdrawal; the emperor issued an edict rebuking him and demoted him to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Guolin delayed submitting his retirement memorial, the emperor rebuked him by edict and demoted him to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was restored to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 國麟乞引退，不許。

translations.literal: Guolin begged to withdraw; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin again asked to retire, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，復以請，上不悅，命奪官，在咸安宮效力。

translations.literal: After several months he petitioned once more; the emperor was displeased and ordered his rank stripped, assigning him to serve at Xian'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he renewed his plea; the emperor, angered, stripped him of rank and assigned him to menial duty at Xian'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 八年，乃許其還裡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was at last permitted to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was finally allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詣京師祝上壽，賜禮部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he came to the capital to offer birthday congratulations and was granted the rank of Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he traveled to the capital for the emperor's birthday and received the honorary rank of Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 田從典，字克五，山西陽城人。

translations.literal: Tian Congdian, whose style was Kewu, was a native of Yangcheng in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Congdian, courtesy name Kewu, came from Yangcheng in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 父雨時，明諸生。

translations.literal: His father Yushi was a licentiate of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yushi had been a Ming dynasty licentiate.

sentences.zh: 寇亂，挈子及兄之孤徙避，度不能兼顧，棄子負兄子以走。

translations.literal: During the bandit turmoil he took his son and his elder brother's orphan and moved to escape; judging that he could not care for both, he abandoned his son and carried his brother's son as he fled.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits ravaged the region he fled with his son and his brother's orphaned boy; unable to save both, he left his own son behind and carried his nephew on his back.

sentences.zh: 賊退，求得子草間，即從典也。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew he found his son in the grass—this was Congdian.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits withdrew he found his son alive in the grass: the boy who would become Congdian.

sentences.zh: 從典篤學，以宋五子為宗。

translations.literal: Congdian was devoted to learning and took the Five Masters of Song as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Congdian studied with deep devotion in the tradition of the Song Neo-Confucian masters.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年，成進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 旋居父喪，事必遵家禮。

translations.literal: He soon entered mourning for his father and in all matters strictly followed the family rites.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately entered mourning for his father and observed every detail of the family rites.

sentences.zh: 服終，就選。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he entered the selection queue for office.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he entered the queue for official appointment.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，授廣東英德知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was appointed magistrate of Yingde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was posted as magistrate of Yingde in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 縣地瘠，賦籍不可稽，詭寄逋逃，民重困。

translations.literal: The county land was barren; tax registers could not be verified; false registration and tax evasion left the people heavily burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Yingde was poor country with unreliable tax rolls; false registration and evasion had crushed the people under double burdens.

sentences.zh: 陋例兩加至八九錢，名曰「均平」。

translations.literal: A corrupt custom added surcharges twice, reaching eight or nine cash, called "equalization."
translations.idiomatic: A corrupt surcharge called "equalization" had been levied twice over, adding eight or nine cash to every assessment.

sentences.zh: 從典盡革之，清其籍。

translations.literal: Congdian abolished all of these and cleared the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Congdian abolished every such levy and rebuilt the tax registers.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，行取，四十三年，授雲南道御史。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was selected for capital service; in the forty-third year he was appointed censor of the Yunnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for capital service in the forty-second year, he became Yunnan Circuit Censor the year after.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「督撫不拘成例，請調州縣，有秉公者，即有徇私者。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "When governors-general and governors, disregarding precedent, request transfers of prefects and magistrates, where there are those who act impartially, there are also those who act from private interest.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that when governors-general and governors bypassed rules to shuffle prefects and magistrates, impartial transfers were always paired with self-serving ones.

sentences.zh: 州縣求調，其弊有三：圖優缺，避衝繁，預為卓薦地。

translations.literal: When prefects and magistrates seek transfer, the abuses are three: seeking lucrative posts, avoiding difficult and busy ones, and securing ground for outstanding recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who sought transfers did so for three reasons: to land easy, lucrative posts; to dodge hard assignments; or to position themselves for preferential promotion.

sentences.zh: 督撫濫調，其弊亦有三：徇請託，得賄賂，引用其私人。

translations.literal: When governors-general and governors transfer officials recklessly, the abuses are likewise three: indulging requests from patrons, taking bribes, and installing their own men.
translations.idiomatic: Governors who abused transfer power did so to honor patrons, take bribes, or install their own clients.

sentences.zh: 名為整頓地方，簡拔賢良，實乃巧開捷徑。

translations.literal: In name it is to put local administration in order and select the worthy; in reality it is a clever shortcut.
translations.idiomatic: Such transfers were billed as reform and merit selection but were in truth a back door to advancement.

sentences.zh: 屢經敗露，有駭聽聞。

translations.literal: Repeated exposures have been shocking to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Scandals had erupted again and again, each more shocking than the last.

sentences.zh: 嗣後請除江、浙等省一百一十餘縣錢糧難徵，及邊遠煙瘴地，仍舊例調補，其他不准濫調。」

translations.literal: Hereafter, except for the more than one hundred and ten counties in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and other provinces where tax collection is difficult, and remote malarial regions, which may still be filled by transfer according to old precedent, other cases should not permit reckless transfer."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that only the 110-odd Jiangsu and Zhejiang counties with hard-to-collect taxes, plus remote malarial districts, retain the old transfer practice; everywhere else reckless shuffling should be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「京官考選科道，令部院堂官保送，恐平日之交結，臨時之營謀，在所難免。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "When capital officials are examined and selected for censorial posts, having ministry and court heads recommend them raises fears that everyday connections and last-minute scheming cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: In a second memorial he argued that letting ministry chiefs nominate censorial candidates invited favor-trading and last-minute intrigue.

sentences.zh: 請敕吏部，遇考選科道，凡正途部屬，及自知縣升任中、行、評、博，與翰林一體論俸開列，聽候考選。」

translations.literal: He requested that the Board of Civil Appointments be ordered: whenever censorial posts are filled by examination, all regular-route subordinates of ministries, together with middle, acting, reviewing, and erudite officials promoted from magistracies, should, like Hanlin members, be listed by seniority of salary and await examination and selection."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that the Board of Civil Appointments list all regular-route ministry officials and magistrates promoted to middle, acting, reviewing, or erudite posts by salary seniority—on the same footing as Hanlin scholars—for open competitive selection.

sentences.zh: 均下部議行。

translations.literal: Both memorials were referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals went to the ministry for deliberation and enactment.

sentences.zh: 巡視西城，罷鋪墊費。

translations.literal: While inspecting the Western City he abolished shop padding fees.
translations.idiomatic: During his inspection of the Western City he abolished padding fees extorted from shopkeepers.

sentences.zh: 察通州倉儲，僦神祠以居，廟祝不受值，不入也。

translations.literal: While inspecting Tongzhou granaries he rented a shrine to lodge in; the temple keeper would accept no payment, and he would not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting Tongzhou granaries, he rented a shrine for lodging but refused to enter when the caretaker would take no rent.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，擢通政司參議。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Transmission Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he was promoted to vice director of the Transmission Office.

sentences.zh: 屢遷轉授光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: After repeated transfers he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Further promotions eventually brought him to the directorship of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 寺故有買辦人，虧戶部帑至四十一萬餘，從典請限年帶銷。

translations.literal: The court had long employed purchasing agents who had depleted the Ministry of Revenue treasury by more than four hundred and ten thousand taels; Congdian requested amortization over a fixed term.
translations.idiomatic: Purchasing agents at the court had run up a deficit of more than 410,000 taels against the Ministry of Revenue; Congdian asked that the debt be written off in annual installments.

sentences.zh: 遷左副都御史，再遷兵部侍郎，並命兼領光祿寺。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, then again to Vice Minister of War, and in both cases was also ordered concurrently to direct the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, then Vice Minister of War, retaining charge of the Court of Imperial Entertainments throughout.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he became Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督常鼐疏言安徽布政使年希堯、鳳陽知府蔣國正婪取，為屬吏所訐。

translations.literal: Governor-General Chang Nai memorialized that Anhui Provincial Commissioner Nian Xiyao and Fengyang Prefect Jiang Guozheng had been greedy in exaction and were impeached by subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Chang Nai reported that Anhui Commissioner Nian Xiyao and Fengyang Prefect Jiang Guozheng had extorted their subordinates, who had impeached them.

sentences.zh: 命從典與副都御史屠沂往按，國正坐斬，希堯奪官。

translations.literal: Congdian was ordered to investigate together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Tu Yi; Guozheng was sentenced to decapitation and Xiyao was stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Congdian and Vice Censor-in-Chief Tu Yi were sent to investigate; Jiang Guozheng was condemned to execution and Nian Xiyao dismissed.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he became Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng's first year he moved to the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 二年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the second year he served as Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 三年，授文華殿大學士，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, concurrently serving as Minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered the Grand Secretariat as Wenhua Hall Grand Secretary while heading the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，乞休，優詔褒許，加太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year he requested retirement; an edict of praise graciously granted it, and he was made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent upon retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year he asked to retire; the emperor praised him warmly, granted the request, and invested him as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 賜宴於居第，令部院堂官並集，發帑治裝，行日，百官祖餞，馳驛歸里，驛道二十里內有司送迎。

translations.literal: A banquet was granted at his residence; ministry and court heads were all ordered to assemble; treasury funds were issued for travel expenses; on the day of departure officials saw him off; he traveled by courier post back home, and within twenty li of the post road local officials escorted him.
translations.idiomatic: The court feasted him at home, summoned every ministry chief to attend, paid his travel expenses from the treasury, and on departure day officials lined the road; he rode the courier post home while local magistrates escorted him for twenty li along the route.

sentences.zh: 入辭，賜禦榜聯並冠服、朝珠。

translations.literal: When he came to take leave he was granted an imperial couplet for his hall, together with court dress and court beads.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor bestowed an imperial couplet, court robes, and court beads.

sentences.zh: 四月乃行，甫一舍，次良鄉，病大作，遂卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He set out in the fourth month; after only one stop he lodged at Liangxiang, fell gravely ill, and died at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He left in the fourth month but had gone only one stage when he fell seriously ill at Liangxiang and died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 上聞，以從典子懋幼，遣內閣學士一、侍讀學士一為治喪，散秩大臣一、侍衛六奠茶酒，並命地方官送其喪歸里。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, considering Congdian's son Mao was young, he dispatched one Grand Secretary and one Reader-in-Waiting to manage the funeral, one minister without portfolio and six guards to offer libations, and also ordered local officials to escort the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Congdian's son Mao was still a boy, the emperor sent a grand secretary and a reader-in-waiting to manage the funeral, a minister without portfolio and six guards to pour libations, and ordered local officials to escort the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 賜祭葬，諡文端。

translations.literal: Imperial funeral rites were granted, and he was posthumously titled Wende.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted state funeral honors and posthumously titled him Wende.

sentences.zh: 懋，自廕生授刑部員外郎，世宗命改吏部，遷郎中，授貴州道御史。

translations.literal: Mao, starting as a yin graduate, was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments; the Yongzheng Emperor ordered him transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments; he was promoted to Director and appointed censor of the Guizhou circuit.
