translations.idiomatic: Mao entered service through the yin privilege as a vice director in the Ministry of Punishments; Yongzheng moved him to the Board of Civil Appointments, where he rose to director and then Guizhou Circuit Censor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，遷禮科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he was transferred to Supervising Secretary of the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he became supervising secretary of the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 疏言河南秋審寬縱，巡撫尹會一、按察使隋人鵬下吏議。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Henan's autumn review of capital cases was too lenient; Governor Yin Huiyi and Provincial Judge Sui Renpeng were referred to officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He charged that Henan's autumn judicial review was unduly lenient; Governor Yin Huiyi and Provincial Judge Sui Renpeng were referred for disciplinary review.

sentences.zh: 又劾工部尚書趙弘恩受賕，奪官，戍軍台。

translations.literal: He also impeached Minister of Works Zhao Hong'en for taking bribes; Zhao was stripped of rank and sent to serve at a military penal colony.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Minister of Works Zhao Hong'en for bribery; Zhao was dismissed and banished to a military penal colony.

sentences.zh: 遷鰿臚寺少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Honglu Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 高宗獎懋敢言，超擢副都御史。

translations.literal: The Qianlong Emperor praised Mao for daring to speak and promoted him directly to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong commended Mao's outspokenness and leapfrogged him to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments and then to the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Minister of Punishments, then moved to the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上責懋奏事每漏言，且嗜酒務博，命解任歸里讀書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the emperor rebuked Mao for leaking matters whenever he memorialized, and for loving wine and gambling; he was ordered dismissed and sent home to study.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the emperor scolded Mao for leaking confidential business in his memorials and for drinking and gambling; he was dismissed and sent home to study.

sentences.zh: 十四年，召授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was recalled and appointed vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 以僕從鬥毆傷人，責懋舊習未悛，仍命歸里讀書。

translations.literal: Because his servants fought and injured someone, Mao was rebuked for old habits unchanged and again ordered home to study.
translations.idiomatic: When his servants brawled and wounded a man, the emperor blamed Mao for failing to reform and sent him home to study once more.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for twenty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He spent twenty years in retirement before he died.

sentences.zh: 高其位，字宜之，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Gao Qiwei, whose style was Yizhi, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qiwei, courtesy name Yizhi, was a Han Chinese bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父天爵，語在​​忠義傳。

translations.literal: His father Tianjue is treated in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tianjue's biography appears among the Loyalty and Righteousness biographies.

sentences.zh: 其位初隸鑲白旗，自筆帖式管佐領。

translations.literal: Qiwei was originally registered in the Bordered White Banner and rose from clerk to assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Qiwei began in the Bordered White Banner, rising from clerk to assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，以署參領從軍駐襄陽。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign, as acting commandant he joined the army and was stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he campaigned as acting commandant and was garrisoned at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 叛將楊來嘉、王會等以二萬人出掠，將攻南漳，其位率二十騎覘敵，與遇，越敵隊入南漳，與共守，敵圍攻不能下。

translations.literal: The rebel generals Yang Laijia, Wang Hui, and others led twenty thousand men out to raid and were about to attack Nanzhang; Qiwei led twenty horsemen to reconnoiter the enemy, encountered them, passed through their ranks into Nanzhang, and defended it together with the garrison; the enemy besieged and attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals Yang Laijia and Wang Hui raided with twenty thousand men toward Nanzhang; Qiwei rode out with twenty scouts, cut through the enemy column into the city, and helped hold the walls until the rebels gave up the siege.

sentences.zh: 叛將譚弘以三萬人犯鄖陽，其位將百人扼楊谿鋪，與相持七十餘日。

translations.literal: The rebel general Tan Hong invaded Yunyang with thirty thousand men; Qiwei commanded a hundred men to hold Yangxi Post and held out against him for more than seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel general Tan Hong marched thirty thousand men against Yunyang, Qiwei blocked Yangxi Post with a hundred troops and held for more than seventy days.

sentences.zh: 糧盡，煮馬韉以食。

translations.literal: When grain was exhausted they boiled horse trappings for food.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions ran out they boiled horse trappings to eat.

sentences.zh: 副都統李麟隆援至，合擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Vice Commander-in-Chief Li Linlong arrived with relief; they joined attack and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander-in-Chief Li Linlong arrived with reinforcements, and together they routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 尋追論禦敵穀城失利，奪官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward a retrospective inquiry judged his defense at Gucheng a failure, and his rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: A later review blamed him for the defeat at Gucheng, and he was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 久之，授火器營操練校尉，襲其祖尚義二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was appointed drill captain of the Firearms Brigade and inherited his grandfather Shangyi's second-class ada hafan rank.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was made drill captain in the Firearms Brigade and inherited his grandfather Shangyi's second-class ada hafan title.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍裕親王福全討噶爾丹，戰於烏闌布通，破駱駝營，擢參領。

translations.literal: He followed the Grand General, Prince Fu, in the campaign against Galdan; at the battle of Ulan Butung he broke the camel camp and was promoted to commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning under Grand General Prince Fu against Galdan, he smashed the camel formation at Ulan Butung and was promoted to commandant.

sentences.zh: 授甘肅永昌副將。

translations.literal: He was appointed deputy commander at Yongchang in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted deputy commander at Yongchang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 明法令，築堡塞，邊境肅清。

translations.literal: He clarified laws and orders, built fortresses and passes, and the border was cleared and settled.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced discipline, built fortifications, and brought the frontier under control.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣襄陽總兵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regional commander at Xiangyang in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted regional commander at Xiangyang in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 擢提督，賜孔雀翎、櫜鞬、鞍馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief and granted a peacock feather, bow-and-quiver case, and saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to provincial commander-in-chief, he received a peacock feather, bow case, and saddle horse from the throne.

sentences.zh: 調江南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: His command was moved to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督常鼐有疾，上命其位署理。

translations.literal: Governor-General Chang Nai was ill, and the emperor ordered Qiwei to serve as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Chang Nai fell ill, the emperor had Qiwei act in his place.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，召入覲，旋命回提督任。

translations.literal: When the Yongzheng Emperor took the throne, Qiwei was summoned to audience and soon afterward ordered back to his post as provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng summoned him to court on accession, then sent him back to his command.

sentences.zh: 奏請保護聖躬，上褒其有愛君之心，溫詔嘉許。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to protect the sacred person of the emperor; the emperor praised his heart of love for the ruler and granted a warm edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized pledging to guard the emperor's person; Yongzheng praised his loyalty and answered with a warm commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年秋，奏飛鴉食蝗，秋禾豐茂。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Yongzheng he memorialized that flying crows ate locusts and the autumn grain grew lush.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he reported that crows had devoured the locusts and the autumn crop was thriving.

sentences.zh: 上以蝗不成災，傳示王大臣，賜詩褒之。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that the locusts had not become a disaster, circulated the report among princes and grand ministers and granted a poem in praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor circulated the good news among princes and senior ministers and rewarded him with a commendatory poem.

sentences.zh: 冬，奏進黃浦漁人網得雙夔龍紐未刻玉印，上賜以四團龍補服。

translations.literal: In winter he memorialized presenting a jade seal with twin kui-dragon knobs, uncarved, netted by fishermen on the Huangpu; the emperor granted him a four-clawed dragon rank badge.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he presented an uncarved jade seal with twin dragon knobs that Huangpu fishermen had hauled in; the emperor bestowed a four-clawed dragon rank badge.

sentences.zh: 三年，授文淵閣大學士，兼禮部尚書，加太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Pavilion of the Deep Pool, concurrently serving as Minister of Rites, and was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered the Grand Secretariat as Wenyuan Pavilion Grand Secretary, headed the Ministry of Rites, and was named Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以衰老辭，不許。

translations.literal: He declined on grounds of old age; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded old age, but the emperor would not release him.

sentences.zh: 改隸鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 賜壽，賚榜聯及白金千。

translations.literal: Birthday honors were granted, together with a couplet for his hall and a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: On his birthday the court granted him a hall couplet and a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 屢乞休，乃命以原官致仕。

translations.literal: After repeated requests for retirement he was at last ordered to retire at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: After many petitions he was finally allowed to retire with his full rank intact.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，賜祭葬，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; imperial funeral rites were granted, and he was posthumously titled Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year; the court granted state funeral honors and posthumously titled him Wenke.

sentences.zh: 子高起，以廕生授四川茂州知州。

translations.literal: His son Gao Qi, starting as a yin graduate, was appointed magistrate of Maozhou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao Qi entered service through the yin privilege as magistrate of Maozhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部尚書，坐事奪官逮治。

translations.literal: He was promoted by stages to Minister of War; for an offense he was stripped of office and arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Minister of War, but an official offense cost him his post and led to arrest and prosecution.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，戍軍台，釋回。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he was sent to serve at a military penal colony, then released and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianlong years he was banished to a military penal colony before being pardoned and allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 遜柱，棟鄂氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhu, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhu, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 曾祖郎色，太祖時，從其兄郎格來歸。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Langse, during the Taizu reign, came to submit together with his elder brother Lange.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Langse submitted to the dynasty in the Taizu era together with his elder brother Lange.

sentences.zh: 遜柱初授筆帖式，擢工部主事。

translations.literal: Sun Zhu was first appointed a clerk, then promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhu began as a clerk and was promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 再遷戶部郎中，授御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to department director in the Ministry of Revenue and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was next transferred to department director in the Ministry of Revenue and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 歷翰林院侍讀學士、內閣學士、盛京工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, grand secretary, and vice minister of the Mukden Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Hanlin reader-in-waiting, grand secretary, and vice minister of the Mukden Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 召改吏部，擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital, moved to the Ministry of Personnel, and promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，署大學士，旋授文淵閣大學士，仍兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he served as acting grand secretary; soon he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Pavilion of the Deep Pool, still concurrently minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In 1727 he served as acting grand secretary and was soon made Wenyuan Pavilion Grand Secretary while retaining the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 遜柱長兵部十六年，屢陳奏部政，多所考覈釐正。

translations.literal: Sun Zhu headed the Ministry of War for sixteen years, repeatedly memorializing on departmental affairs and undertaking many examinations, verifications, and corrections.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhu ran the Ministry of War for sixteen years, repeatedly memorializing on its affairs and conducting extensive reviews and reforms.

sentences.zh: 十年，以老，命不必兼兵部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, on grounds of age, he was ordered no longer to hold the Ministry of War concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In 1732, citing old age, he was relieved of his concurrent post at the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十一年，致仕，卒，年八十四，諭褒遜柱「醇厚和平」，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he retired; he died at age eighty-four. An edict praised Sun Zhu as "honest, generous, and conciliatory," and imperial funeral rites were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in 1733 and died at eighty-four. The court praised him as "sincere, mild, and peaceable" and granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 尹泰，章佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Yin Tai, of the Zhangjia clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tai, of the Zhangjia clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授翰林院筆帖式，再遷內閣侍讀。

translations.literal: At first appointed a Hanlin clerk, he was transferred again to Grand Secretariat reader.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Hanlin clerk and was later transferred to reader in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年，授翰林院侍講，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed Hanlin expositor and served as diarist of the Daily Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1688 he became Hanlin expositor and was appointed diarist of the Daily Lecture.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，授國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was appointed chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1695 he was appointed chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，改錦州佐領。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to assistant commandant at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1698 he was transferred to assistant commandant at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，以病罷，遂居錦州。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was dismissed on grounds of illness and thereafter lived at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1713 illness forced his retirement, and he settled in Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗在籓邸，奉命詣奉天謁陵，過錦州宿焉，與語奇之，見其子尹繼善。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor was still in his prince's residence, ordered to go to Fengtian to visit the imperial tombs, he passed Jinzhou and lodged there; speaking with Yin Tai he regarded him as remarkable and met his son Yin Jishan.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Yongzheng emperor was still a prince, he was ordered to visit the imperial tombs at Fengtian. Passing through Jinzhou, he stayed overnight with Yin Tai, was deeply impressed by their conversation, and met Yin Jishan.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，召授內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was summoned and appointed grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1723 he was summoned to court and appointed grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎，再遷左都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of works, then again to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of works and then to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「六科書吏，賄通提塘，造為小鈔、晚帖，內開口傳諭旨，或誤繙清文，甚至偽造上有賜予及與諸臣問對，應請禁止。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The clerks of the Six Offices of Scrutiny bribe the courier stations to produce small notices and evening bulletins containing orally transmitted edicts, sometimes mistranslating Manchu documents, and even forging imperial grants and exchanges between the throne and ministers. This should be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that clerks in the Six Offices of Scrutiny were bribing courier stations to circulate small notices and evening bulletins purporting to carry orally transmitted edicts, sometimes botching Manchu translations and even forging imperial gifts and exchanges between the emperor and his ministers, and he asked that the practice be banned.

sentences.zh: 二年，充會典總裁。

translations.literal: In the second year he served as chief compiler of the Collected Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1724 he was appointed chief compiler of the Collected Statutes.

sentences.zh: 三年，命以原品署盛京侍郎，兼領奉天府尹。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered, at his original rank, to serve as acting vice minister at Mukden while concurrently heading the Fengtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1725 he was ordered to serve at his existing rank as acting Mukden vice minister while also serving as prefect of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「承德等九州縣原徵豆米，多貯無用。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The beans and rice originally levied from the nine prefectures and counties around Chengde are mostly stored without use.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the beans and rice levied from the nine prefectures and counties around Chengde were largely stockpiled to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 請自雍正四年始，停徵黑豆，按畝徵米，按丁徵銀，而以原貯米豆視時價出糶。」

translations.literal: He requested that from the fourth year of Yongzheng the levy of black beans be stopped, that rice be levied by mu and silver by household, and that the grain and beans already stored be sold according to current prices."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that from 1726 the black-bean levy be abolished, that rice be collected by acre and silver by household, and that existing stores be sold off at prevailing prices.

sentences.zh: 又言：「關東風高土燥，請掘地窖藏存穀，以節建倉工費。」

translations.literal: He further stated: "In the Eastern Pass region the winds are strong and the soil dry; he requested that underground pits be dug to store grain, so as to save the labor and expense of building granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that in Manchuria, where winds are strong and the soil dry, grain should be stored in underground pits to avoid the cost of building granaries.

translations.literal: (Close of memorial quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (Close of memorial quotation.)

sentences.zh: 四年，山海關總管多索禮疏言應交莊頭餘地，尹泰不即派官丈收。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the commandant-general of Shanhaiguan, Duosuoli, memorialized that surplus land of estate managers should be turned over; Yin Tai did not immediately dispatch officials to measure and receive it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1726 Shanhaiguan commandant-general Duosuoli memorialized that surplus estate-manager land should be surrendered, but Yin Tai did not promptly send officials to survey and take possession.

sentences.zh: 命侍郎查郎阿往按，坐解府尹任，仍以左都御史協理奉天將軍。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Chalang'a was ordered to investigate; Yin Tai was punished by removal from the prefecture, but still served as left censor-in-chief assisting the general of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Vice Minister Chalang'a to investigate. Yin Tai was removed as prefect but continued as left censor-in-chief assisting the Fengtian general.

sentences.zh: 將軍噶爾議設外海水師，尹泰以為旅順、天津俱有水師，錦、复、蓋諸州亦可更番巡察，增設需費浩繁，於巡察無益。

translations.literal: General Gar proposed establishing coastal naval forces; Yin Tai held that Lüshun and Tianjin already had naval units, and that Jinzhou, Fuxing, and Gaizhou could also be patrolled in rotation, while adding new forces would require vast expense and bring no benefit to patrol duties.
translations.idiomatic: When General Gar proposed establishing a coastal navy, Yin Tai argued that Lüshun and Tianjin already had naval forces and that Jinzhou, Fuxing, and Gaizhou could be covered by rotating patrols; new units would cost a fortune and do little for coastal surveillance.

sentences.zh: 別疏以聞。

translations.literal: He submitted a separate memorial to report this.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a separate memorial setting out his view.

sentences.zh: 下議政王大臣議，如尹泰言。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Deliberative Council of Princes and High Officials, which agreed with Yin Tai.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Deliberative Council, which sided with Yin Tai.

sentences.zh: 六年，坐遺漏入官財產，奪官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, for failing to report property that should have been confiscated for the state, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728 he was dismissed for failing to report property due for confiscation to the state.

sentences.zh: 尋命复官。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to office.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，與尚書陳元龍同授額外大學士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year he was, together with Minister Chen Yuanlong, appointed Extra Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1729 he and Minister Chen Yuanlong were appointed Extra Grand Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 尋授東閣大學士，兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, concurrently serving as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Dongge Grand Secretary while retaining the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十三年，高宗即位，充世宗實錄總裁。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Gaozong Emperor acceded, he served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Shizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1735, when the Qianlong emperor came to the throne, he was appointed chief compiler of the Yongzheng emperor's veritable records.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，以老病乞罷，上留之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, on grounds of old age and illness he requested dismissal; the emperor kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he asked to retire on account of age and illness, but the emperor kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善自兩江總督入覲，授刑部尚書，俾使朝夕侍養。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan came from the Liangjiang governor-generalship to attend audience and was appointed Minister of Punishments, so that he might attend his father morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan came from Liangjiang to audience and was appointed Minister of Punishments so that he could care for his father day and night.

sentences.zh: 三年，复乞罷，命以原官致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year he again requested dismissal and was ordered to retire at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1738 he again asked to retire and was permitted to leave office with his full rank.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，賜祭葬，諡文恪。

translations.literal: Soon he died; imperial funeral rites were granted, and he was posthumously titled Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after; the court granted state funeral honors and posthumously titled him Wenke.

sentences.zh: 尹繼善自有傳。

translations.literal: Yin Jishan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jishan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 陳元龍，字廣陵，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Yuanlong, style name Guangling, was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanlong, courtesy name Guangling, was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十四年一甲二名進士，授編修，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi he ranked second in the first class of jinshi, was appointed compiler, and served in the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: In 1685 he placed second in the first class of jinshi, was appointed Hanlin compiler, and entered the Southern Studio.

sentences.zh: 郭琇劾高士奇，辭連元龍，謂與士奇結為叔侄，招納賄賂，命與士奇等並休致。

translations.literal: When Guo Xiu impeached Gao Shiqi, his language implicated Yuanlong, alleging that he and Shiqi had formed an uncle-nephew bond and accepted bribes; he was ordered, together with Shiqi and others, to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Xiu impeached Gao Shiqi, he implicated Yuanlong as well, claiming the two had entered a corrupt uncle-nephew relationship and taken bribes. Yuanlong was ordered to retire along with Shiqi and the others.

sentences.zh: 語互詳士奇傳。

translations.literal: The details are given in full in the biography of Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recounted at length in Gao Shiqi's biography.

sentences.zh: 元龍奏辯，謂：「臣宗本出自高，譜牒炳然。

translations.literal: Yuanlong memorialized in his defense, saying: "My clan originally derives from the Gao family, and the genealogies are clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlong defended himself in a memorial: "My clan truly descends from the Gao line, and the genealogical records are explicit.

sentences.zh: 若果臣交結士奇，何以士奇反稱臣為叔？」

translations.literal: If I had indeed colluded with Shiqi, why would Shiqi in turn call me uncle?"
translations.idiomatic: If I had truly colluded with Shiqi, why would he have addressed me as his uncle?"

sentences.zh: 事得白，命復任。

translations.literal: The matter was cleared; he was ordered restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The case was cleared and he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted by stages to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 元龍工書，為聖祖所賞，嘗命就御前作書，深被獎許。

translations.literal: Yuanlong was skilled at calligraphy and was appreciated by the Shengzu Emperor; he was once ordered to write before the throne and was deeply praised and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlong was an accomplished calligrapher whom the Kangxi emperor admired. He was once ordered to write in the imperial presence and was warmly praised.

sentences.zh: 上御便殿書賜內直翰林，諭曰：「爾等家中各有堂名，不妨自言，當書以賜。」

translations.literal: The emperor, writing in a side hall, granted calligraphy to the Hanlin on inner duty and instructed them: "Each of you has a hall name at home; you may speak of it yourselves, and I shall write it as a gift."
translations.idiomatic: Writing in a side hall, the emperor granted calligraphy to the Hanlin on inner duty and said: "Each of you has a hall name at home. Tell me yours, and I shall write it for you.

sentences.zh: 元龍奏臣父之闓年逾八十，家有愛日堂，御書榜賜之。

translations.literal: Yuanlong memorialized that his father Zhikai was over eighty and that the family hall was called the Hall of Cherishing the Sun; the emperor wrote a plaque and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlong replied that his father Zhikai was over eighty and that the family hall was called the Hall of Cherishing the Sun. The emperor wrote a plaque and bestowed it.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，再遷詹事。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was transferred again to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1703 he was promoted to tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 以父病乞養歸，賜葠。

translations.literal: On grounds of his father's illness he requested leave to return home and care for him; ginseng was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill he asked to return home to care for him and was granted ginseng as a gift.

sentences.zh: 時正編賦匯，令攜歸校對增益。

translations.literal: At the time the Collected Fu was being compiled; he was ordered to take it home to collate and augment.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then compiling the Collected Fu and ordered him to take the draft home to revise and supplement it.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，元龍迎謁，御書榜賜之闓及元龍母陸。

translations.literal: When the emperor made a southern tour, Yuanlong came forward to greet him; imperial calligraphy was granted to Zhikai and to Yuanlong's mother, Lady Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the south, Yuanlong came forward to greet him. The emperor granted calligraphy to Zhikai and to Yuanlong's mother, Lady Lu.

sentences.zh: 之闓卒，喪終，召元龍授翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: When Zhikai died and the mourning period ended, Yuanlong was summoned and appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhikai died and Yuanlong completed mourning, he was recalled and appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 五十年，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he was transferred to vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1711 he was transferred to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 授廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was named governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 值廣東歲歉，廣西米價高，元龍遣官詣湖南採米平糶。

translations.literal: When Guangdong suffered a poor harvest and grain prices in Guangxi were high, Yuanlong dispatched officials to Hunan to procure rice and sell it at fair prices.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong had a poor harvest and Guangxi grain prices rose, Yuanlong sent officials to Hunan to buy rice and sell it at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，修築興安陡河閘，護兩廣運道。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he repaired the Xing'an steep-river sluice gate to protect the transport route of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1715 he repaired the Xing'an steep-river sluice gate to safeguard the Guangdong-Guangxi transport route.

sentences.zh: 並於省城擴養濟院，立義學，創育嬰堂，建倉貯穀。

translations.literal: He also expanded the poor-relief hospice in the provincial capital, established charity schools, founded a foundling hospital, and built granaries to store grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the provincial capital he also expanded the poor-relief hospice, founded charity schools and a foundling hospital, and built granaries.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1718 he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 六十年，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1721 he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，命守護景陵。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded, he was ordered to guard the Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng emperor came to the throne, he was ordered to serve as guardian of the Yongzheng mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 七年，與左都御史尹泰同授額外大學士，尋授文淵閣大學士，兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was, together with Left Censor-in-Chief Yin Tai, appointed Extra Grand Secretary; soon he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Pavilion of the Deep Pool, concurrently serving as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1729 he and Left Censor-in-Chief Yin Tai were appointed Extra Grand Secretaries; he was soon made Wenyuan Pavilion Grand Secretary while retaining the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 元龍在廣西，請開例民捐穀得入監。

translations.literal: While Yuanlong was in Guangxi, he requested that a precedent be opened for commoners to donate grain and thereby enter the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Guangxi, Yuanlong proposed allowing commoners to enter the Imperial Academy by donating grain.

sentences.zh: 李紱為巡撫，請以捐穀為開墾費。

translations.literal: When Li Fu became governor, he requested that donated grain be used as funds for opening new land.
translations.idiomatic: His successor Li Fu asked that donated grain be spent on land reclamation.

sentences.zh: 上責其借名支銷，命元龍詣廣西清理。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for using the scheme as a pretext to draw funds, and ordered Yuanlong to go to Guangxi to settle the accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Li for spending the funds under false pretenses and ordered Yuanlong to Guangxi to straighten out the accounts.

sentences.zh: 紱旋奏：「元龍分得羨餘十一萬有奇，除在廣西捐公費九萬，又助軍需十萬。

translations.literal: Li Fu soon memorialized: "Yuanlong received a surplus share of more than 110,000 taels; apart from donating 90,000 taels for public expenses in Guangxi, he also contributed 100,000 taels for military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu soon reported that Yuanlong had received a surplus share of more than 110,000 taels, of which he had donated 90,000 taels for public expenses in Guangxi and another 100,000 taels for military supplies.

sentences.zh: 今倉穀尚有虧空，應令分償。」

translations.literal: The granary grain still shows a deficit, and he should be ordered to make restitution in proportion."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the granary accounts still showed a shortfall, and he should be made to repay his share.

sentences.zh: 及授大學士，命免之。

translations.literal: When he was appointed grand secretary, the order for restitution was waived.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanlong was appointed grand secretary, the emperor waived the demand for repayment.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以老乞休，加太子太傅致仕，令其子編修邦直歸侍養。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on grounds of age he requested retirement; he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and retired, and his son the compiler Bangzhi was ordered home to attend to him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1733 he asked to retire on account of age, was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and was allowed to leave office; his son Bangzhi, a Hanlin compiler, was sent home to care for him.

sentences.zh: 行日，賜酒膳，令六部滿、漢堂官餞送，沿途將吏送迎。

translations.literal: On the day of his departure wine and food were granted, the Manchu and Chinese department heads of the Six Ministries were ordered to see him off, and local officials along the route were to escort and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left the capital he was granted wine and food, the Manchu and Chinese heads of the Six Ministries were ordered to give him a farewell banquet, and officials along the route were to receive him.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，命在籍食俸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was ordered to draw salary while at home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he was permitted to draw his salary while living at home.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，賜祭葬，諡文簡。

translations.literal: Soon he died; imperial funeral rites were granted, and he was posthumously titled Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after; the court granted state funeral honors and posthumously titled him Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 論曰：軾以德望尊，徐元夢以忠謇重。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Shi was honored for moral stature, and Xu Yuanmeng was esteemed for unwavering loyalty and frankness.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Zhu Shi was revered for moral authority, and Xu Yuanmeng for steadfast loyalty and blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 世宗譴允禩、允禟，徐元夢言：「二人罪當誅，原上念手足情緩其死。」

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor punished Yin Zhi and Yin Tang, Xu Yuanmeng said: "The two men's crimes merited execution; I pray that Your Majesty, mindful of brotherly affection, may temper their punishment and spare their lives."
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng emperor moved against Yin Zhi and Yin Tang, Xu Yuanmeng pleaded: "Their crimes deserve death, but I beg Your Majesty, out of brotherly feeling, to spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 二人者既死，吏議奴其子，軾言：「二人子實為聖祖孫，孰敢奴之？」

translations.literal: After the two men died, the officials proposed enslaving their sons; Shi said: "The sons of the two men are in truth grandsons of the Holy Ancestor—who would dare enslave them?"
translations.idiomatic: After the two princes died, officials proposed reducing their sons to servitude. Zhu Shi objected: "They are the Kangxi emperor's grandsons—who would dare treat them as slaves?"

sentences.zh: 世宗皆為動容。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor was moved in both cases.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng emperor was deeply moved on both occasions.

sentences.zh: 諒哉，古大臣不是過也。

translations.literal: How discerning! Such ancient great ministers were not surpassed by this.
translations.idiomatic: How discerning they were—worthy of the great ministers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 廷錫直內廷領戶部，邁柱等領疆節，卓然有績效。

translations.literal: Tingxi attended the inner court while heading the Ministry of Revenue, and Mai Zhu and others held frontier command; all achieved marked results.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tingxi served in the inner court while running the Ministry of Revenue, and Mai Zhu and others held frontier commands—all with clear achievement.

sentences.zh: 從典、尹泰皆以端謹奉職。

translations.literal: Congdian and Yin Tai both served their offices with upright conscientiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Congdian and Yin Tai both discharged their duties with upright diligence.

sentences.zh: 古所謂大人長者，殆近之矣。

translations.literal: What the ancients called great men and elders of character—they probably come close to this.
translations.idiomatic: In the ancients' phrase, "great men and elders of character"—these men surely come close.
